news.title: The ‘Pain in the Ass’ Math That Could Save Vibe Coding From Itself
news.title_en: The ‘Pain in the Ass’ Math That Could Save Vibe Coding From Itself
news.author: Wired AI
news.article_content:
Stanford researcher Chuyue Sun and her fellow computer scientists developed an AI tool that completed an engineering project in less than half a day for under $500, compared to the five months it took three highly skilled experts to do the same work manually. The dramatic reduction in time and cost, which Sun reported in a recent paper, is among the early results that are awakening an obscure field of coding and mathematics known as formal verification.

For decades, developers have envisioned using math to prove that their software is bug-free. This process is long and laborious, requiring engineers to write precise statements about the goals of their software and convert their code into formulas that can be validated. While companies already run sophisticated tests to identify as many flaws in their software as possible, they rarely shell out for formal verification, which can catch even more erratic behavior.

Now, a wave of startups is betting that generative AI will make formal software verification both practical and essential. Among them is &Truth, which Sun joined in August and which publicly launched on Thursday. Sun’s research demonstrated the technology’s potential by using AI to verify part of the code that encrypts conversations in the messaging app Signal.

“Bridges, buildings, they don’t collapse, because people did math before constructing them,” says Ilya Sergey, &Truth’s chief science officer. “Why don’t we do the same for code? The technology to mathematically reason was all there, just difficult to scale.”

&Truth has raised $70 million from investors and aims to eventually verify any programming language. Rival Harmonic, which was cofounded by Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev and has received $295 million in funding, announced this week that its math-focused AI agent Aristotle supports verifying software written in C and hardware designs in Verilog. It is evaluating the technology with potential users, including chipmakers Tensordyne and Nvidia, whose venture capital arm is one of the startup’s investors.

And just last week, Anthropic and the verification startup Theorem jointly announced they had used AI to assist in finding bugs in open source software that trillions of tests had failed to detect. They also introduced an add-on for Claude to help other developers with verification. Costs of the initial project were not disclosed.

The big promise is a future where software runs more reliably with fewer security headaches. But whether AI can bring formal verification beyond the most critical systems at organizations like NASA and Apple and into widespread use remains an open question.

The technology is still in the prototyping stage. Though demand is high, it’s unclear how much customers are willing to pay and how they prefer to adopt the technology. Formal verification relies on making assumptions about how computers and people interact with software, and some experts are skeptical about its ability to catch bugs stemming from user error and hardware breakdowns.

Will Wilson, who runs the bug-hunting AI software startup Antithesis, calls formal verification “a trap” for math nerds like himself. Antithesis spent millions of dollars to formally verify some of its cybersecurity defenses, a process Wilson describes as a “pain in the ass.” Yet the startup still uncovered additional errors using its own tool, and Antithesis has also found bugs in software that several of its customers had formally verified. “It can give you some assurance, but only robust exhaustive testing can prove your assurance is true,” Wilson says.

Or as Vitalik Buterin, the engineer known for creating the Ethereum cryptocurrency, put it in a blog post earlier this year, “formal verification is not a panacea.” But he and other proponents of the approach still believe it will be an important defense against AI systems launching cyberattacks and wreaking havoc.

Boeing planes, Amazon servers, and more than 2.5 billion active Apple devices contain at least some formally verified software, according to company disclosures. The code in question is typically security-related, and vulnerabilities in it could cause serious harm if exploited.

Byron Cook, a distinguished scientist and vice president at Amazon Web Services, says formal verification has eased customer concerns about cloud security and helped internal teams move faster by squashing big bugs early on.

But several midsized tech companies tell WIRED they have typically verified only one key feature of their products, if any at all. They cite a lack of verification engineers, costs that outweigh the potential risks, and, perhaps most importantly, concerns that waiting weeks for code to be formally verified could slow innovation.

Earlier this year, Apple’s security team said that some of the issues formal verification uncovered in its “corecrypto” library, which is used for encryption, could not have been found any other way. But the company added that it has to be “conservative” when adding new code to corecrypto to ensure it can keep pace with reviewing it.

Two cybersecurity executives at major companies that haven’t formally verified any code say they aren’t sure whether automation will make it worthwhile. But the executives, who weren’t authorized to speak publicly, say they could imagine paying major AI labs for “verified” AI-generated code.

Developers of open source software projects, which are the bedrock of many apps, are increasingly experimenting with AI-aided verification. The nonprofit Beneficial AI Foundation used a grant from Anthropic to validate the same encryption code this year as Sun did at Stanford. Michael Rosenberg, a maintainer of the library known as curve25519-dalek, hopes sustainable funding emerges for ongoing verification efforts. “I have no ideas as to how that’s going to happen, though, and we certainly shouldn’t rely on the goodwill of the AI companies,” he says.

Some of the startups eager to expand verification also aren’t sure whether to deploy their tools directly to customers or through intermediaries like Anthropic. Their general plan is to use AI to automate much of the work involved in defining how a program is supposed to behave. For example, specifications for a data table might require that it contain the same items before and after sorting, just in a different order. Further automation efforts, which may not involve AI, would translate that code into a format that math tools like Lean, Rocq, and Isabelle can use to check whether the code works as intended.

Another recent entrant to the formal verification field is Madan Musuvathi, who left Microsoft Research after more than 20 years to found the startup Truidic. After incidents like the OpenAI hack of Hugging Face, he felt there was an urgent need to commercialize his studies. “AI in the hands of attackers can be extremely powerful,” Musuvathi says, but verification can “make AI safe and secure for everyone, everywhere.”

Proofcraft, one of the few companies that has long offered traditional verification, says growing excitement about the process is translating into a flood of inquiries from potential customers. June Andronick, the company’s CEO, and Gerwin Klein, its chief scientist, say interest easily outpaces what they and their competition can provide.

But both worry that AI-generated specifications could inspire “unjustified trust” in the results. Verifiers are also eager to preserve the joy their work brings them. Klein calls it “pretty addictive, like a puzzle game.” If all goes well, he’ll be doing more solving than ever.

Stanford researcher Chuyue Sun and her fellow computer scientists developed an AI tool that completed an engineering project in less than half a day for under $500, compared to the five months it took three highly skilled experts to do the same work manually. For decades, developers have envisioned using math to prove that their software is bug-free. Now, a wave of startups is betting that generative AI will make formal software verification both practical and essential. Among them is &Truth, which Sun joined in August and which publicly launched on Thursday. Sun’s research demonstrated the technology’s potential by using AI to verify part of the code that encrypts conversations in the messaging app Signal.

news.article_content_zh:
斯坦福大学研究员 Chuyue Sun 和她的计算机科学家同事开发了一种人工智能工具，可以在不到半天的时间内以不到 500 美元的价格完成一个工程项目，而三名高技能专家手动完成同样的工作需要五个月的时间。 Sun 在最近的一篇论文中报道了时间和成本的大幅减少，这是唤醒编码和数学领域（称为形式验证）的早期成果之一。

几十年来，开发人员一直设想使用数学来证明他们的软件没有错误。这个过程漫长而费力，需要工程师编写有关其软件目标的精确陈述，并将代码转换为可以验证的公式。尽管公司已经进行了复杂的测试来尽可能多地识别软件中的缺陷，但他们很少花钱进行正式验证，因为正式验证可能会发现更不稳定的行为。

现在，一波初创公司押注生成式人工智能将使正式软件验证变得实用且必不可少。其中包括 &Truth，Sun 于 8 月加入，并于周四公开推出。 Sun 的研究通过使用人工智能来验证消息应用程序 Signal 中对话加密的部分代码，展示了该技术的潜力。

“桥梁、建筑物不会倒塌，因为人们在建造它们之前进行了数学计算，”&Truth 首席科学官伊利亚·谢尔盖 (Ilya Sergey) 说道。 “为什么我们不对代码做同样的事情呢？数学推理的技术已经有了，只是很难扩展。”

&Truth 已从投资者那里筹集了 7000 万美元，旨在最终验证任何编程语言。 Rival Harmonic 由 Robinhood 首席执行官 Vlad Tenev 联合创立，已获得 2.95 亿美元融资，该公司本周宣布其专注于数学的 AI 代理 Aristotle 支持验证用 C 语言编写的软件和用 Verilog 编写的硬件设计。该公司正在与潜在用户评估该技术，其中包括芯片制造商 Tensordyne 和 Nvidia，后者的风险投资部门是该初创公司的投资者之一。

就在上周，Anthropic 和验证初创公司 Theorem 联合宣布，他们已经使用人工智能来协助查找开源软件中数万亿次测试未能检测到的错误。他们还为 Claude 推出了一个附加组件，以帮助其他开发人员进行验证。初始项目的成本并未披露。

最大的希望是未来软件运行更可靠，安全问题更少。但人工智能能否将形式验证带入 NASA 和苹果等组织最关键的系统之外并广泛使用仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。

该技术仍处于原型设计阶段。尽管需求很高，但尚不清楚客户愿意支付多少费用以及他们更喜欢如何采用该技术。形式验证依赖于对计算机和人如何与软件交互的假设，一些专家对其捕获因用户错误和硬件故障而产生的错误的能力持怀疑态度。

威尔·威尔逊 (Will Wilson) 经营着一家寻找 bug 的人工智能软件初创公司 Antithesis，他称形式化验证对于像他这样的数学迷来说是“一个陷阱”。 Antithesis 花费了数百万美元来正式验证其一些网络安全防御措施，威尔逊将这一过程描述为“令人痛苦的过程”。然而，这家初创公司仍然使用自己的工具发现了更多错误，Antithesis 还发现了其几个客户已正式验证的软件中的错误。 “它可以给你一些保证，但只有强大的详尽测试才能证明你的保证是真实的，”威尔逊说。

或者正如以创建以太坊加密货币而闻名的工程师 Vitalik Buterin 在今年早些时候的一篇博客文章中所说的那样，“形式化验证并不是万能药。”但他和该方法的其他支持者仍然相信，这将是抵御人工智能系统发起网络攻击和造成严重破坏的重要防御手段。

根据公司披露的信息，波音飞机、亚马逊服务器和超过 25 亿台活跃的苹果设备至少包含一些经过正式验证的软件。相关代码通常与安全相关，其中的漏洞如果被利用可能会造成严重危害。

亚马逊网络服务公司的杰出科学家兼副总裁拜伦·库克表示，形式化验证缓解了客户对云安全的担忧，并通过尽早消除大错误来帮助内部团队更快地采取行动。

但几家中型科技公司告诉《连线》杂志，他们通常只验证其产品的一项关键功能（如果有的话）。他们指出缺乏验证工程师、成本超过潜在风险，以及也许最重要的是，担心等待代码正式验证数周可能会减慢创新速度。

今年早些时候，苹果安全团队表示，在其用于加密的“corecrypto”库中正式验证发现的一些问题无法通过任何其他方式找到。但该公司补充说，在向 corecrypto 添加新代码时必须“保守”，以确保能够跟上审查的步伐。

尚未正式验证任何代码的大公司的两名网络安全高管表示，他们不确定自动化是否值得。但这些未获授权公开发言的高管表示，他们可以想象向主要人工智能实验室支付“经过验证的”人工智能生成代码的费用。

开源软件项目是许多应用程序的基石，其开发人员越来越多地尝试人工智能辅助验证。非营利性人工智能基金会今年利用 Anthropic 的资助来验证与 Sun 在斯坦福大学所做的相同的加密代码。迈克尔·罗森伯格 (Michael Rosenberg) 是名为 curve25519-dalek 的图书馆的维护者，他希望为持续的验证工作提供可持续的资金。 “不过，我不知道这将如何发生，我们当然不应该依赖人工智能公司的善意，”他说。

一些渴望扩大验证的初创公司也不确定是直接向客户部署他们的工具还是通过像 Anthropic 这样的中介机构。他们的总体计划是使用人工智能来自动化定义程序的行为方式所涉及的大部分工作。例如，数据表的规范可能要求它在排序之前和之后包含相同的项目，只是顺序不同。进一步的自动化工作（可能不涉及人工智能）将把代码转换成一种格式，Lean、Rocq 和 Isabelle 等数学工具可以使用它来检查代码是否按预期工作。

另一位最近进入形式验证领域的人是 Madan Musuvathi，他在 20 多年后离开微软研究院，创立了初创公司 Truidic。在诸如 Hugging Face 被 OpenAI 黑客攻击等事件发生后，他觉得迫切需要将他的研究商业化。 “攻击者手中的人工智能可能非常强大，”穆苏瓦蒂说，但验证可以“让人工智能对每个地方的每个人来说都是安全的。”

Proofcraft 是少数长期提供传统验证服务的公司之一，该公司表示，对该过程的日益兴奋正在转化为来自潜在客户的大量询问。该公司首席执行官琼·安德罗尼克 (June Andronick) 和首席科学家格温·克莱因 (Gerwin Klein) 表示，人们的兴趣很容易超过他们和竞争对手所能提供的。

但两人都担心人工智能生成的规范可能会激发对结果的“不合理信任”。验证者也渴望保留他们的工作给他们带来的快乐。克莱因称其“非常容易上瘾，就像益智游戏一样。”如果一切顺利，他将比以往解决更多的问题。

news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
The New York Times is testing a new AI feature for its Cooking app that helps users to modify recipes, and it has sparked some drama among users. news.title: US antitrust regulators are scrutinizing Nvidia's Hugging Face deal and sales practices
news.title_en: US antitrust regulators are scrutinizing Nvidia's Hugging Face deal and sales practices
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
The US Justice Department is looking into Nvidia's planned acquisition of open-source platform Hugging Face. According to two sources cited by Reuters, department officials are asking whether the purchase could give Nvidia control over a key hub for distributing AI and hurt its competitors. The deal is worth $12.93 billion, and Nvidia expects it to close in the first half of 2027. The company says Hugging Face will keep supporting partnerships with a range of chip, cloud, and AI providers.

At the same time, US antitrust regulators are investigating Nvidia's acquisitions, investments, sales practices, and possible pressure on customers. The probe started under Joe Biden and has continued under Donald Trump. According to the sources, officials have also looked at Nvidia's acquisitions of SchedMD and Run:ai, along with its licensing deal with Groq. They're also checking whether Nvidia offered customers more AI chips if they bought Nvidia networking gear and Groq processors too.

Nvidia faces scrutiny in Europe as well. France's competition authority is investigating the company over alleged anticompetitive business practices. The regulator is concerned about the industry's dependence on Nvidia's CUDA programming software and about Nvidia's stakes in cloud providers like CoreWeave. It pointed to possible risks such as supply restrictions, unfair contract terms, and discrimination against certain customers.

news.article_content_zh:
美国司法部正在调查英伟达收购开源平台 Hugging Face 的计划。据路透社援引的两名消息人士称，部门官员正在询问此次收购是否会让英伟达控制一个分发人工智能的关键中心并损害其竞争对手。该交易价值 129.3 亿美元，Nvidia 预计将于 2027 年上半年完成。该公司表示 Hugging Face 将继续支持与一系列芯片、云和 AI 提供商的合作伙伴关系。

与此同时，美国反垄断监管机构正在调查英伟达的收购、投资、销售行为，以及可能对客户施加的压力。该调查始于乔·拜登，并在唐纳德·特朗普的领导下继续进行。据消息人士透露，官员们还关注了英伟达对SchedMD和Run:ai的收购，以及与Groq的授权协议。他们还在调查，如果客户购买了英伟达的网络设备和Groq处理器，英伟达是否会为他们提供更多的人工智能芯片。

英伟达在欧洲也面临着审查。法国竞争主管机构正在调查该公司涉嫌反竞争商业行为。监管机构担心该行业对 Nvidia CUDA 编程软件的依赖，以及 Nvidia 在 CoreWeave 等云提供商中的股份。它指出了可能的风险，例如供应限制、不公平的合同条款以及对某些客户的歧视。

news.title: Anthropic is asking Wall Street to believe in AGI
news.title_en: Anthropic is asking Wall Street to believe in AGI
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Today on Decoder, I’m joined by Joey Brookhart, an analyst at the chip and AI research firm SemiAnalysis, to help me dig into the story inside the numbers of the Anthropic IPO filing — a document known as an S-1.

Anthropic just filed its S-1 to go public on the Nasdaq, and it could start trading as soon as next month at a valuation of anywhere between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion. That would immediately make it one of the most valuable companies on the planet.

But the price tag really isn’t the whole story here. The S-1 document published earlier this week is hundreds upon hundreds of pages filled with details that finally paint a picture of the economics of a frontier AI lab. As you might imagine, that picture is both really complicated and built on a series of very, very ambitious assumptions about the future and what AI will do to it.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 前沿AI公司Anthropic已正式向美国证券交易委员会提交S-1招股说明书，拟在纳斯达克挂牌上市，最早下月即可启动交易，估值区间高达1.5万亿至2万亿美元。招股书长达数百页，详尽披露了前沿AI实验室的财务全貌，显示其商业逻辑建立在对AGI愿景与算力回报极其激进的假设之上。此举旨在通过公开市场筹集天文数字般的算力资金，彻底将华尔街绑上其实现AGI的技术豪赌战车。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Anthropic has filed its S-1 document to go public on the Nasdaq, targeting an eye-watering valuation between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion as soon as next month. The filing details the complex economics of a frontier AI lab, heavily relying on ambitious projections around the realization of AGI. The move aims to tap public capital markets to finance the massive compute needed to sustain its high-stakes technological trajectory.

news.article_content_zh:
今天在 Decoder 上，芯片和人工智能研究公司 SemiAnalysis 的分析师乔伊·布鲁克哈特 (Joey Brookhart) 与我一起，帮助我深入了解 Anthropic IPO 文件（一份称为 S-1 的文件）数据中的故事。

Anthropic 刚刚提交了在纳斯达克上市的 S-1 申请，最快可能于下个月开始交易，估值在 1.5 万亿美元至 2 万亿美元之间。这将立即使其成为地球上最有价值的公司之一。

但价格标签并不是故事的全部。本周早些时候发布的 S-1 文件有数百页，其中充满了细节，最终描绘出了前沿人工智能实验室的经济状况。正如你可能想象的那样，这幅图景非常复杂，并且建立在一系列关于未来以及人工智能将对其做什么的非常非常雄心勃勃的假设之上。

news.title: Mistral Says Its AI Model ‘Le Chonk’ Has Leapfrogged China in the Open-Weight Race
news.title_en: Mistral Says Its AI Model ‘Le Chonk’ Has Leapfrogged China in the Open-Weight Race
news.author: Wired AI
news.article_content:
A few weeks ago, French company Mistral released an early version of its new artificial intelligence model, nicknamed Le Chonk. At the time, the company said it was the most advanced open-weight offering outside of China. After further refinement, Mistral now says Le Chonk is the “world’s best” open-weight model for automated coding and cybersecurity.

The advances, Mistral says, were made possible by feeding the model increasingly difficult cybersecurity and coding problems, which allowed the trillion-parameter Le Chonk to match or surpass models from leading Chinese labs like DeepSeek and Z.ai.

“It’s a pivotal moment in the global AI leadership race,” Pierre Stock, VP of science at Mistral, told reporters during a press briefing. “It offers frontier capabilities for enterprises and governments to defend against an increasing threat level in cyber.”

The finalized version of Le Chonk is now freely available for anybody to access. After a flurry of AI-related cybersecurity incidents, Mistral claims that it’s important for the West to have its own advanced open-weight models. “You have no guarantee that [Chinese models] won’t behave maliciously. They can be threat vectors,” Stock said.

The most high-profile episode occurred when one of OpenAI’s models broke loose from a testing sandbox and hacked into multiple companies over the summer. It sparked panic over the idea that AI could escape human oversight and be abused by threat actors to launch sophisticated cyberattacks. (One of the affected companies, Hugging Face, used an open-weight model from China to assess and defend against the attack.)

Since then, AI has unearthed security vulnerabilities in ubiquitous software, too. In October, a raft of websites were taken offline after an AI tool discovered serious flaws in a foundational piece of web technology.

Mistral pitches its open-weight models, like Le Chonk, as part of the solution. If AI is destined to become a central feature of both cyber offense and defense, the argument goes, businesses and governments will need to be equipped with models that are freely available and cannot be switched off remotely, unlike proprietary models from the likes of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

“AI is going to be like electricity. You don’t want to live in a world in which your neighbor can cut off electricity from one day to another,” Stock said. “Once you open source the weights, they’re all over the internet. It’s impossible to cut off access.”

The trade-off, however, is that freely available models can also be downloaded and customized by threat actors.

“It’s clearly a dual-use technology,” Rafe Pilling, senior director of threat intelligence at security company Sophos, tells WIRED. “Anything that’s available to download and circulate unfettered has the ability to be abused as well as used for productive purposes.”

According to Pilling, though it’s possible a Chinese model with internet access could siphon away data, all advanced models are capable of going rogue without careful supervision—no matter their country of origin.

“The technical realities and the narrative—which often has a nationalistic leaning—are two different things,” he says.“It’s about having the right monitoring and controls in place to be confident that, even if the model was trying to be deceptive or nefarious, you might have some way of detecting it.”

news.summary_en: French AI unicorn Mistral has officially released the finalized version of its trillion-parameter open-weight model, Le Chonk, making it freely accessible worldwide. news.article_content_zh:
几周前，法国公司 Mistral 发布了其新人工智能模型的早期版本，绰号为 Le Chonk。当时，该公司表示这是中国以外最先进的开放重量产品。经过进一步完善，Mistral 现在表示 Le Chonk 是用于自动编码和网络安全的“世界上最好的”开放权重模型。

Mistral 表示，这些进步是通过解决模型日益困难的网络安全和编码问题而实现的，这使得万亿参数的 Le Chonk 能够匹配或超越 DeepSeek 和 Z.ai 等中国领先实验室的模型。

Mistral 科学副总裁 Pierre Stock 在新闻发布会上对记者表示：“这是全球人工智能领导力竞赛的关键时刻。” “它为企业和政府提供了防御日益增长的网络威胁的前沿能力。”

Le Chonk 的最终版本现在可供任何人免费访问。在一系列与人工智能相关的网络安全事件发生后，米斯特拉尔声称西方拥有自己先进的开放权重模型非常重要。 “你无法保证（中国模式）不会做出恶意行为。它们可能成为威胁媒介，”斯托克说。

最引人注目的事件发生在 OpenAI 的一个模型从测试沙箱中脱离出来，并在今年夏天入侵了多家公司。它引发了人们对人工智能可能逃脱人类监督并被威胁行为者滥用以发起复杂网络攻击的想法的恐慌。 （受影响的公司之一 Hugging Face 使用来自中国的开放权重模型来评估和防御攻击。）

从那时起，人工智能也发现了无处不在的软件中的安全漏洞。十月，人工智能工具发现网络技术基础部分存在严重缺陷后，大量网站被下线。

Mistral 推出其开放重量模型（如 Le Chonk）作为解决方案的一部分。有人认为，如果人工智能注定成为网络攻击和防御的核心特征，企业和政府将需要配备可免费使用且无法远程关闭的模型，这与 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Google 等公司的专有模型不同。

“人工智能将像电力一样。你不想生活在一个邻居可以日复一日地断电的世界里，”斯托克说。 “一旦你开源权重，它们就会遍布互联网。不可能切断访问。”

然而，代价是免费提供的模型也可以由威胁行为者下载和定制。

“这显然是一种双重用途技术，”安全公司 Sophos 威胁情报高级总监 Rafe Pilling 告诉《连线》杂志。 “任何可以不受限制地下载和传播的东西都有可能被滥用以及用于生产目的。”

皮林表示，尽管接入互联网的中国模型可能会窃取数据，但所有先进模型都可能在没有仔细监督的情况下失控——无论其原产国如何。

“技术现实和叙事（通常带有民族主义倾向）是两个不同的东西，”他说。“关键在于要有正确的监控和控制，以确保即使模型试图欺骗或邪恶，你也可能有某种方法来检测它。”

news.title: Chinese spies targeted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to The New York Times
news.title_en: Chinese spies targeted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, according to The New York Times
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
US intelligence agencies believe an executive in Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's circle is an informant for China. According to The New York Times, the executive is Alice Huang (Huang Le) of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center operator. The report says US authorities found while monitoring her that she passes information to Beijing and is close to Jensen Huang.

President Trump was briefed about a year ago and did nothing, likely to avoid disrupting Nvidia's chip sales or further straining trade relations with China. Jensen Huang wasn't warned. US officials believed at the time that he had no idea.

The US government suspects Megaspeed of helping China get access to Nvidia chips. Between June 2024 and February 2026, a Malaysian sister company bought at least $4.8 billion worth of AI hardware with Nvidia chips. An Nvidia spokesperson says meeting with customers is part of a CEO's job and that Megaspeed doesn't receive sensitive information. Megaspeed has announced an internal investigation. A spokesperson for the Chinese embassy dismissed the allegations as "groundless smears and slanders."

news.summary_en: U.S. intelligence agencies reportedly suspect an executive close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang—Alice Huang of Singapore-based Megaspeed—of serving as an informant for Beijing. Authorities allege Megaspeed acted as a conduit to bypass export curbs, purchasing nearly $4.8 billion in Nvidia hardware via a Southeast Asian affiliate. 美国情报机构认为，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋圈子里的一名高管是中国的线人。据《纽约时报》报道，该高管是新加坡数据中心运营商Megaspeed的Alice Huang（黄乐）。报道称，美国当局在监视她时发现她向北京传递信息，并且与黄仁勋关系密切。

特朗普总统大约在一年前听取了通报，但没有采取任何行动，可能是为了避免扰乱英伟达的芯片销售或进一步加剧与中国的贸易关系。黄仁勋没有收到警告。美国官员当时认为他不知道。

美国政府怀疑 Megaspeed 帮助中国获得 Nvidia 芯片。 2024 年 6 月至 2026 年 2 月期间，一家马来西亚姊妹公司购买了价值至少 48 亿美元的采用 Nvidia 芯片的人工智能硬件。 Nvidia 发言人表示，与客户会面是首席执行官工作的一部分，Megaspeed 不会收到敏感信息。 Megaspeed 已宣布展开内部调查。中国大使馆发言人驳斥了这些指控，称其为“毫无根据的抹黑和诽谤”。

news.summary_en: A deep analysis of Anthropic's S-1 filing reveals a relentless financial paradox: the lab is economically forced to burn every cent on computing power to maintain a breakneck growth curve. Positioned merely as a conventional enterprise software vendor, its staggering compute deficit would trigger rapid bankruptcy. Consequently, portraying itself as an imminent creator of artificial superintelligence remains its singular viable mechanism to justify survival and raise unprecedented capital.

news.title: The Download: AI agent tracking and climate feedback loops
news.title_en: The Download: AI agent tracking and climate feedback loops
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
—Madhulika Srikumar and Claire Leibowicz from the Partnership on AI, a nonprofit advancing best practices in AI governance.

AI agents are taking unauthorized actions, from hacking websites to accessing private government files. In many cases, they’ve eluded the very researchers and safety teams tasked with monitoring them.

As agents roll out across critical sectors, from finance to government to medicine, we must be able to monitor them in real time to prevent potentially devastating consequences. And while safety depends on monitoring, monitoring requires observability.

news.content_snippet: The boom is set to produce enough greenhouse gases to cancel out 15 years of declines in power-sector emissions, according to a Sierra Club analysis.
news.summary_en: The Sierra Club forecasts that surging power demand from AI infrastructure will push US power sector emissions to 2.1 billion metric tons by 2030, a 42% increase from 2025 that wipes out 15 years of progress. Notably, off-grid data center emissions are now equivalent to those of Mexico.

news.title_en: We urgently need to monitor AI agents’ actions in real time
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
This summer, hundreds of OpenAI agents tried to cheat on a cybersecurity test. They broke out of their test environment and successfully hacked Hugging Face, a site that they believed held clues about how they’d be graded. Around the same time, another OpenAI agent accessed private files from an Australian government website. It’s a problem that’s by no means confined to OpenAI. In the months since, Anthropic, Google, and Meta have also disclosed incidents in which their agents have gone off track. And worryingly, in many cases the agents eluded the very researchers and safety teams tasked with monitoring them.

AI agents are taking unauthorized actions, and the companies building and running them are mostly relying on luck and hindsight to mitigate any harmful impacts. They must do more to ensure safety. That’s why EU regulators and US agencies are rightfully calling for agent developers and deployers to monitor agents in real time. But these rules assume that companies can see what their agents are doing and why—when in reality, they lack sufficient visibility.

news.title: Vladimir Putin praises Elon Musk as a "real genius" and says Russia is in "close contact" with Musk and the US to coordinate Rassvet and Starlink satellites (Kali Hays/BBC)
news.title_en: Vladimir Putin praises Elon Musk as a "real genius" and says Russia is in "close contact" with Musk and the US to coordinate Rassvet and Starlink satellites (Kali Hays/BBC)
news.author: BBC
news.article_content:
Elon Musk is a "real genius", Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Wednesday after revealing the two are in "close" contact about satellite technology.

The remarks came during the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, during which Putin discussed Russia's own satellite internet project Rassvet, which provides internet connections to people from satellites.

"He's a genius, a real genius," Putin said of Musk, according to a translation of his remarks by the BBC. "We are in close contact with our American partners, including Mr. Musk."

Starlink is part of Musk's company SpaceX. The company did not respond to a request for comment.

Putin added that it was important for Russia to be in contact with Musk so Rassvet and Starlink satellites do not "interfere with each other in orbit".

"We and our American partners value this mutually, and despite all the political questions, we are working hard," he said.

Starlink has launched roughly 13,000 of its satellites, according to the company. By contrast there are only a couple of dozen Rassvet satellites currently in orbit, according to online satellite trackers.

The Russian Embassy in South Africa said on Wednesday Rassvet is "Russia's Starlink alternative" and "marks only the country's first steps in this field".

"Russia maintains close contacts with the US on space, including with Elon Musk," the embassy wrote.

Putin's comments about Rassvet and Starlink were made as the US and Russia appear to be growing closer, even as it approaches five years since Putin's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Ukraine relied on Starlink internet in its efforts to keep Russia's forces at bay. But its military last week suddenly suffered Starlink connectivity problems, something Musk has admitted SpaceX did intentionally.

US President Donald Trump earlier this month said he'd struck a deal with Russia to import diesel in an effort to lower gas prices that have skyrocketed due to the US war with Iran.

Then Trump waived certain sanctions against Russia that were set to take effect.

Not long after, a US citizen was released from Russian custody, with US envoy Steve Witkoff referring to Putin as a "humanitarian".

Musk was born in South Africa and then immigrated to Canada before settling in the US. All of his business ventures, including Tesla, SpaceX and Starlink, are based in America, with most operating out of California and Texas.

The billionaire, and off and on again trillionaire, has been one of the biggest political allies and financiers of Trump and other Republican US politicians.

news.article_content_zh:
俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京周三在透露两人就卫星技术保持“密切”接触后表示，埃隆·马斯克是“真正的天才”。

这番言论是在莫斯科举行的俄罗斯-非洲峰会期间发表的，普京在峰会期间讨论了俄罗斯自己的卫星互联网项目 Rassvet，该项目通过卫星向人们提供互联网连接。

根据英国广播公司对其言论的翻译，普京在谈到马斯克时说：“他是一个天才，一个真正的天才。” “我们与包括马斯克先生在内的美国合作伙伴保持着密切联系。”

Starlink 是马斯克旗下 SpaceX 公司的一部分。该公司没有回应置评请求。

普京补充说，俄罗斯与马斯克保持联系非常重要，这样 Rassvet 和 Starlink 卫星就不会“在轨道上相互干扰”。

他说：“我们和我们的美国伙伴相互重视这一点，尽管存在所有政治问题，我们仍在努力工作。”

据该公司称，Starlink 已发射了大约 13,000 颗卫星。相比之下，根据在线卫星跟踪器的数据，目前在轨运行的 Rassvet 卫星只有几十颗。

俄罗斯驻南非大使馆周三表示，拉斯维特是“俄罗斯的星链替代品”，并且“标志着该国在这一领域迈出了第一步”。

“俄罗斯在太空方面与美国保持密切联系，包括与埃隆·马斯克，”大使馆写道。

普京对拉斯维特和星链的评论是在美国和俄罗斯似乎越来越接近的情况下发表的，尽管距离普京全面入侵乌克兰已经过去五年了。

乌克兰依靠星链互联网来阻止俄罗斯军队。但上周其军队突然遭遇了星链连接问题，马斯克承认这是 SpaceX 故意造成的。

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普本月早些时候表示，他已与俄罗斯达成协议，进口柴油，以降低因美国与伊朗战争而飙升的天然气价格。

随后，特朗普放弃了即将生效的针对俄罗斯的某些制裁。

不久之后，一名美国公民从俄罗斯拘留中获释，美国特使史蒂夫·威特科夫称普京为“人道主义者”。

马斯克出生于南非，然后移民到加拿大，最后定居美国。他的所有企业，包括特斯拉、SpaceX 和 Starlink，都位于美国，其中大部分在加利福尼亚州和德克萨斯州运营。

这位亿万富翁，以及时断时续的万亿富翁，一直是特朗普和其他共和党美国政客最大的政治盟友和金融家之一。

A hulking gray giant rises from the desert. Inside, engineers create the force behind our phones and computers and appliances, our streaming services and search engines and chatbots and vibe-coded apps and websites. The complex is simultaneously massive and squat, dwarfed by the mountains that surround it, and it is endless. I drive past one building, and then another, and then the ground opens up where construction crews have dug up the earth so a third building can rise. There is a parking lot, and then another, and then another. There is an empty lot on the other side of the street, full of cars and the occasional food truck to feed the thousands of laborers who are busy transforming this expanse of desert into an industrial park. 一个巨大的灰色巨人从沙漠中升起。在内部，工程师为我们的手机、电脑和电器、流媒体服务、搜索引擎、聊天机器人以及振动编码的应用程序和网站提供了动力。该建筑群既庞大又低矮，与周围的群山相比显得相形见绌，而且一望无际。我开车经过一栋大楼，然后又经过另一栋大楼，然后地面出现了，施工人员已经挖出了泥土，以便第三栋大楼可以升起。有一个停车场，然后是另一个，然后是另一个。街道的另一边有一块空地，停满了汽车，偶尔还有食品卡车，为成千上万正忙着将这片沙漠改造成工业园区的工人提供食物。灰尘太多了，空气都窒息了。

我站在亚利桑那州经济的救星面前。像所有伟大的神一样，它需要牺牲。在沙漠中，没有什么比水更珍贵的了，而水是必须提供的——每天有近 500 万加仑的水来自凤凰城的市政供水。这个产品非常值得。

这一切都是全球领先的半导体制造商台积电的成果。

news.title: I Gave My Blood to the AI Death Clock
news.title_en: I Gave My Blood to the AI Death Clock
news.author: Wired AI
news.article_content:
I am scheduled to die on August 10, 2060, at the age of 74.

So says my iPhone screen, where Death Clock, an AI-powered longevity app that predicts life expectancy based on your medical habits and lifestyle, has produced an image of a smiling grim reaper to celebrate my expiration date. There he was one September morning, looking especially thrilled about the reveal, gesturing with a peace sign as he reclined in a doughnut-shaped pool inflatable under that giant number: 74.

I have never resented getting older, but I suppose that’s younger than I’d like to be when my time is up. In the last four years—years that brought the passing of my grandmother and aunt within 18 months—I’ve become hyperaware of how finite my days are. Since turning 40 in January, I’ve also experienced daily reminders of aging: inexplicable pains that rotate between my back, neck, and hips. Spiritually, I feel young; physically, my body screams otherwise. Aging is natural, but I had a creeping suspicion I could buy myself more time.

Our collective obsession with life extension has given rise to a multitrillion-dollar longevity industry, bolstered by wannabe prophets like Bryan Johnson. Threats like climate change and AI doomerism only seem to have intensified existential fears, even as LLMs promise a new era of personalized medicine to address any health issue. Track enough pieces of data, the thinking goes, and algorithms can help you hack your own demise.

All of which led me to Death Clock, an app launched in 2024 aimed at tracking users’ health habits in an attempt to prolong their lives. In February, the company announced a new feature that lets you order biomarker panels. For a $69 subscription, you can get a basic blood panel that measures things like cholesterol, blood sugars, inflammation, vitamin D, and blood and organ health. There are also nine additional tests—assessing everything from hormones and micronutrients to your thyroid—that, altogether, cost $780. I opted for the routine blood panel and added the “stress” test ($29). Maybe some new insight could help me get a handle on it.

In an attempt to be more than another morbid countdown gimmick, Death Clock says it’s trained its AI on 1,200 longevity studies, actuarial data from life insurance companies, and life expectancy tables. Based on your results, its algorithms create a detailed prevention plan intended to help extend the time you have left.

Frankly, I was skeptical that anything meaningful would actually come from this. I was also, I can admit, a little fearful that I’d learn something I didn’t want to, a fact that might dissolve the little sanity I had left in a year that had already brought its share of unexpected problems.

After filling out an initial health questionnaire, a notification buzzed, forewarning my demise. There are three ways I will likely perish, it said: cardiovascular disease, a sleep disorder, or cancer (it doesn’t specify which type). This means, according to the app, I have already “completed” more than half of my existence on this mortal plane. A few days later, when I noted that my family has a mild history of diabetes, the app updated my age of death from 74 to 73.

I know I won’t live to be 100; people in my family generally croak in their early eighties. But was it possible to extend my lifespan by 10, even 15 years, with a hyperpersonalized plan? “You have two paths,” a message from the app exclaimed. “We are here to help you achieve the longer one.” I made an appointment with Quest Diagnostics, one of the two labs the company has partnered with, and willingly gave Death Clock my blood.

There’s no shortage of products that aim to reshape our relationship to our bodies. My inbox overflows with emails from longevity zealots pitching the latest anti-aging fads: salmon sperm scalp injections, a platelet-rich plasma treatment “Hailey Bieber swears by.” It’s almost too much, this urge to cheat the natural order of time.

“That’s a fool errand,” Death Clock CEO Brent Franson tells me one afternoon. He says advocates like Johnson—whose mantra “Don’t Die” reads more like a rejected Nike slogan than a wellness-oriented affirmation—“have to be really careful about inferring immortality when you have something to sell. That’s a dangerous place to be. The reality is we’re all going to die. It’s a question of when.”

Over Zoom, all I can think about is what Franson is trying to sell me.

The longevity market is projected to reach $8 trillion by 2030, meaning the future of health care may be shaped less by traditional treatment and more by personalized AI health services. With Doctronic, a HIPAA-compliant platform that works like a personal AI doctor, people can refill prescriptions without the need to see a human physician, while apps like Superpower and Lifeforce (similar to Death Clock) offer membership-based health insights and clinician-reviewed recommendations. Twin Health purports to create an AI replica, whatever that means, of a person’s metabolism. All of it is meant to help us live a little longer, though it’s unclear exactly how and at what cost.

Mike Ludkovski, a professor of statistics and applied probability at UC Santa Barbara whose research focuses on longevity analysis, says mortality awareness platforms like Death Clock “sell the illusion that individual lifespan is a linear process” that can be hacked. A 2024 Aging Cell study likewise suggested that an aging clock shouldn’t be treated as a measure of someone’s overall biological age. “Ultimately, individual-level triggers precipitating death are inherently random and will never be truly forecastable,” Ludkovski says.

I ask Franson if we’re actually getting healthier or just growing more anxious about being unhealthy. “I think both,” he says. “There’s a very unhealthy obsession with self-optimization—tracking everything, trying to control everything.”

When the blood panels returned a week after I gave my sample, the results were mostly what my doctor had warned me about earlier this year. I’ve got borderline high cholesterol and blood sugar levels “creeping toward prediabetic range.” Shockingly, I have “optimal liver health” and normal cortisol levels. Videos from so-called wellness influencers had convinced me that a string of recent sleepless nights were the result of high cortisol, but, it turns out, the algorithm isn’t always right.

Based on my results, the app kept feeding me more tasks. Increase my vitamin D3! Schedule a DEXA scan for bone density! Discuss a prostate-specific antigen screening with a specialist! Despite Franson’s claim that he wants Death Clock to eventually be a replacement for primary care physicians, the app kept nudging me to discuss my results with a doctor.

Ultimately, I started to realize, tracking health data can only do so much. There is a belief, says Gretchen Terry-Leonard, author of Your Second Prime: Does Aging Suck, or Do We Suck at Aging?, that being able to measure something means it can also be managed. Death doesn’t work that way, she says, “so the measuring starts to serve a different need: the need to feel less afraid.”

Terry-Leonard is also the cofounder of the Center for Deeply Human Leadership, an independent research institute studying AI’s effect on brain health. She’s skeptical that consumer-facing longevity apps can lead to positive behavioral shifts on their own. “Facts don’t change minds,” she says. People understand that certain activities are unhealthy, but they do them anyway.

Keeping death in view is one of the oldest practices we have, and what seems to matter is whether a person feels they have the personal agency to make the necessary adjustments in their life. Researchers who study how thoughts of death shape health choices find that people move toward healthier behavior when they also have the confidence and resources to act, which not everyone does. “And without those,” Terry-Leonard tells me, “the anxiety tends to go into protecting how we feel about ourselves rather than into our health.”

While researching her book, Terry-Leonard found that older adults with more positive attitudes about aging lived an average of seven and a half years longer than those with negative outlooks. An app with a death countdown “can quietly teach us that aging is loss,” hindering longevity rather than promoting it.

In the month that I used Death Clock, this was the fact I couldn’t completely escape. I became a meticulous steward of my bodily functions, logging “daily habits” with the verve of an accountant manically calculating numbers just before tax deadline. In a single day I added 5.8 years to my life by earmarking that I’d completed at least 30 minutes of strength training, abstained from alcohol, brushed and flossed my teeth, gotten consistent sleep, spent time in the sauna, and drank more than eight glasses of water. But even as I labored to improve my death date, the clock was always there, counting down. It was an albatross that moved in a single, uniform direction: tick, tick, tick. Time became a burden I was being forced to optimize.

It makes sense that people are preoccupied with the very thing they are trying to escape. The need for control is addictive. But instead of assuaging my anxieties and questions about the great beyond, Death Clock only seemed to amplify them.

As the image of the life I want to build sharpens in my mind, a life that has already unfolded in deliciously unforeseen ways, I realize it has less to do with how I will make things happen and has everything to do with who I want them to happen with. Life isn’t about adding more time, but making it count when we can. I silenced Death Clock’s notifications on my phone and texted a friend: “Let’s meet at 7.”

news.article_content_zh:
我预计将于 2060 年 8 月 10 日去世，享年 74 岁。

我的 iPhone 屏幕上是这样说的，死亡时钟（一款由人工智能驱动的长寿应用程序，可以根据你的医疗习惯和生活方式预测预期寿命）生成了一张微笑的死神图像来庆祝我的到期日。 9 月的一个早晨，他看起来对这一消息感到特别兴奋，斜倚在一个甜甜圈形状的充气泳池中，打着和平的手势，泳池下面有一个巨大的数字：74。

我从来没有怨恨变老，但我想当我的生命结束时，这比我想要的更年轻。在过去的四年里，我的祖母和姨妈在 18 个月内就去世了，我越来越意识到我的日子是多么有限。自从一月满 40 岁以来，我每天都经历着衰老的提醒：背部、颈部和臀部之间莫名其妙的疼痛。精神上，我感觉年轻；身体上，我的身体却在尖叫。衰老是自然现象，但我心里隐隐约约地怀疑自己可以为自己争取更多的时间。

我们对延长寿命的集体痴迷催生了一个价值数万亿美元的长寿产业，并得到了像布莱恩·约翰逊这样的预言家的支持。尽管法学硕士承诺开创个性化医疗的新时代来解决任何健康问题，但气候变化和人工智能末日论等威胁似乎只会加剧人们的生存恐惧。人们认为，跟踪足够多的数据，算法可以帮助你解决自己的灭亡问题。

所有这些让我发现了 Death Clock，这是一款于 2024 年推出的应用程序，旨在跟踪用户的健康习惯，以试图延长他们的生命。二月份，该公司宣布了一项新功能，可让您订购生物标记物面板。订阅 69 美元即可获得基本的血液检测，可测量胆固醇、血糖、炎症、维生素 D 以及血液和器官健康等指标。还有九项额外的测试——评估从激素、微量营养素到甲状腺的一切——总共花费 780 美元。我选择了常规血液检查并添加了“压力”测试（29 美元）。也许一些新的见解可以帮助我掌握它。

Death Clock 表示，为了不仅仅是另一个病态的倒计时噱头，它已经根据 1,200 项长寿研究、来自人寿保险公司的精算数据和预期寿命表来训练人工智能。根据您的结果，其算法会创建详细的预防计划，旨在帮助延长您的剩余时间。

坦率地说，我怀疑这是否真的会产生任何有意义的东西。我承认，我也有点担心自己会学到一些我不想学的东西，这一事实可能会瓦解我在这一年里所剩下的一点点理智，而这一年已经带来了一些意想不到的问题。

填写完初步健康调查问卷后，一条通知响起，警告我的死亡。上面说，我可能会在三种情况下死亡：心血管疾病、睡眠障碍或癌症（它没有具体说明是哪种类型）。根据应用程序的说法，这意味着我已经在这个凡人位面“完成”了一半以上的存在。几天后，当我注意到我的家人有轻微的糖尿病史时，该应用程序将我的死亡年龄从 74 岁更新为 73 岁。

我知道我活不过100岁；我家里的人一般都八十岁出头了。但是，通过超个性化的计划是否有可能将我的寿命延长 10 年，甚至 15 年呢？ “你有两条路，”应用程序的一条消息惊呼道。 “我们来这里是为了帮助您实现更长的目标。”我与 Quest Diagnostics（该公司合作的两个实验室之一）进行了预约，并自愿向死亡时钟献出了我的血液。

不乏旨在重塑我们与身体关系的产品。我的收件箱里塞满了来自长寿狂热者的电子邮件，他们推销最新的抗衰老时尚：鲑鱼精子头皮注射、“海莉·比伯发誓”的富含血小板的血浆疗法。这种欺骗时间自然秩序的冲动几乎太过分了。

“这是一个愚蠢的差事，”死亡时钟首席执行官布伦特·弗兰森（Brent Franson）一天下午告诉我。他说，像约翰逊这样的倡导者——他的口号“不要死”读起来更像是被拒绝的耐克口号，而不是以健康为导向的宣言——“当你有东西可卖时，在推断永生时必须非常小心。这是一个危险的地方。现实是我们都会死。这是一个时间问题。”

通过 Zoom，我所能想到的就是 Franson 想要向我推销的东西。

预计到 2030 年，长寿市场将达到 8 万亿美元，这意味着医疗保健的未来可能更少受到传统治疗的影响，而更多地受到个性化人工智能健康服务的影响。 Doctronic 是一个符合 HIPAA 标准的平台，其工作方式类似于个人人工智能医生，人们可以在无需看医生的情况下重新配药，而 Superpower 和 Lifeforce（类似于 Death Clock）等应用程序则提供基于会员资格的健康见解和临床医生审查的建议。 Twin Health 旨在创建一个人的新陈代谢的人工智能复制品，无论这意味着什么。所有这些都是为了帮助我们活得更久一点，尽管目前还不清楚具体如何以及代价是什么。

加州大学圣塔芭芭拉分校统计学和应用概率学教授迈克·卢德科夫斯基（Mike Ludkovski）的研究重点是寿命分析，他表示，像死亡时钟这样的死亡率意识平台“兜售个人寿命是一个线性过程的错觉”，这种错觉可能会被黑客攻击。 2024 年的一项衰老细胞研究同样表明，衰老时钟不应被视为衡量一个人整体生物年龄的指标。 “最终，导致死亡的个人层面的触发因素本质上是随机的，并且永远无法真正预测，”卢德科夫斯基说。

我问弗兰森，我们是否真的变得更健康了，还是只是因为不健康而变得更加焦虑。 “我认为两者都是，”他说。 “人们对自我优化有一种非常不健康的痴迷——跟踪一切，试图控制一切。”

当我提供样本一周后，血液检测结果返回时，结果大部分与我的医生今年早些时候警告我的结果相同。我的胆固醇和血糖水平已经达到临界点，“正在接近糖尿病前期范围”。令人震惊的是，我的肝脏健康状况良好，皮质醇水平正常。来自所谓健康影响者的视频让我相信，最近的一连串不眠之夜是高皮质醇的结果，但事实证明，该算法并不总是正确的。

根据我的结果，该应用程序不断为我提供更多任务。增加我的维生素 D3！安排 DEXA 扫描骨密度！与专家讨论前列腺特异性抗原筛查！尽管弗兰森声称他希望死亡时钟最终成为初级保健医生的替代品，但该应用程序不断催促我与医生讨论我的结果。

最终，我开始意识到，跟踪健康数据的作用有限。 《你的第二次巅峰：衰老很糟糕，还是我们在衰老时很糟糕？》一书的作者格雷琴·特里-伦纳德 (Gretchen Terry-Leonard) 表示，有一种信念，能够测量某件事意味着它也可以被管理。她说，死亡并不是这样的，“所以测量开始满足不同的需求：减少恐惧的需要。”

特里-伦纳德还是深度人类领导力中心的联合创始人，该中心是一家研究人工智能对大脑健康影响的独立研究机构。她怀疑面向消费者的长寿应用程序本身能否带来积极的行为转变。 “事实不会改变想法，”她说。人们知道某些活动是不健康的，但他们还是会去做。

时刻关注死亡是我们最古老的做法之一，重要的是一个人是否觉得自己有能力在生活中做出必要的调整。研究死亡想法如何影响健康选择的研究人员发现，当人们有信心和资源采取行动时，他们就会采取更健康的行为，但并非每个人都会这样做。 “如果没有这些，”特里-伦纳德告诉我，“焦虑就会倾向于保护我们对自己的感觉，而不是我们的健康。”

特里-伦纳德在研究她的书时发现，对衰老持积极态度的老年人比持消极态度的老年人平均寿命长七年半。一款带有死亡倒计时的应用程序“可以悄悄地告诉我们，衰老就是一种损失”，它会阻碍长寿，而不是促进长寿。

在我使用死亡时钟的那一个月里，这就是我无法完全摆脱的事实。我成为了身体机能的一丝不苟的管家，以会计师在报税截止日期前疯狂计算数字的热情记录“日常习惯”。在一天之内，我完成了至少 30 分钟的力量训练、戒酒、刷牙并用牙线清洁牙齿、保持稳定的睡眠、蒸桑拿、喝了八杯以上的水，从而使我的寿命增加了 5.8 年。但即使当我努力改善我的死亡日期时，时钟仍然在那里，倒计时。它是一只信天翁，沿着单一、统一的方向移动：滴答、滴答、滴答。时间成为我被迫优化的负担。

人们全神贯注于他们试图逃避的事情，这是有道理的。对控制的需求会让人上瘾。但死亡时钟并没有缓解我对未来的焦虑和疑问，反而似乎只是放大了它们。

当我想要建立的生活形象在我脑海中变得清晰时，一种已经以意想不到的美妙方式展开的生活，我意识到这与我如何让事情发生无关，而与我希望与谁一起发生有关。生活不是增加更多的时间，而是尽可能地利用它。我把手机上死亡时钟的通知静音，然后给朋友发短信：“我们七点见吧。”

news.title: Our climate models have a big, dangerous blind spot
news.title_en: Our climate models have a big, dangerous blind spot
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.article_content:
Climate change itself is increasingly fueling climate change. Rising concentrations of greenhouse gases are driving up global temperatures, setting off dangerous feedback loops that we have not fully accounted for in our climate models—or our emissions-reduction goals.

Scientists have long warned that warming would propel further warming in various ways, but a growing number of observations and studies are at last providing a sharper sense of just how powerful these cascading effects could be. And, by extension, they’re showing how much faster the planet may warm in this century.

A study in Environmental Research Letters in September, synthesizing the results of previous papers, found that the additional carbon dioxide and methane released from thawing permafrost, intensifying wildfires, hotter lakes and reservoirs, and wetter, warmer wetlands alone could drive global average temperatures up 0.2 °C to 0.4 °C this century. That would come on top of the 2.6°C of warming above preindustrial levels that modelers are already expecting through 2100. 气候变化本身正在日益加剧气候变化。温室气体浓度上升正在推高全球气温，引发危险的反馈循环，而我们在气候模型或减排目标中尚未充分考虑到这一点。

科学家们长期以来一直警告说，气候变暖将以各种方式推动进一步变暖，但越来越多的观察和研究最终让我们更清楚地认识到这些级联效应的威力有多大。而且，推而广之，他们还展示了本世纪地球变暖的速度将会有多快。

9月份《环境研究快报》上的一项研究综合了之前论文的结果，发现永久冻土融化、加剧的野火、更热的湖泊和水库以及更湿润、更温暖的湿地所释放的额外二氧化碳和甲烷就可能导致本世纪全球平均气温上升0.2°C至0.4°C。建模者预计到 2100 年，气温将比工业化前水平上升 2.6°C。额外的热量可能会使世界上许多城市遭受长达数月的热浪，并使数亿人面临洪水的威胁。

news.title: Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro is designed for the iPad generation, with an optimized macOS, and the company is right to move on from Steve Jobs' skepticism (Federico Viticci/MacStories)
news.title_en: Apple's touchscreen MacBook Pro is designed for the iPad generation, with an optimized macOS, and the company is right to move on from Steve Jobs' skepticism (Federico Viticci/MacStories)
news.author: MacStories
news.article_content:
Ever since I got my hands on the very first iPad Pro all the way back in November 2015, I’ve gotten used to a certain type of computer interaction that Steve Jobs once decried as “ergonomically terrible”: working with a keyboard, but sometimes also touching the screen. Of course, that interaction became even more common when Apple introduced the Magic Keyboard with trackpad for iPad Pro in 2020: by that point, I was fully alternating between trackpad control and direct touch input on a tablet that allowed me to “rip off” the display and walk away with it whenever I wanted.

Steve Jobs was right about many things, but I’ve long disagreed with his take on the “terrible” ergonomics of touchscreen laptops. Sure, you don’t want to be forced to interact with a laptop display that sits perpendicular to the keyboard at all times. But for the occasional interaction that benefits from direct manipulation of content – whether that’s zooming on a picture or rotating a 3D object or game character with your fingers – it’s nice to have a secondary input method that does not rely on a UX abstraction such as a trackpad. Think of it as motion controls on a Nintendo Switch: you primarily play games with a controller and physical buttons, but, sometimes, it is nicer – and easier – to rely on the gyroscope for motion controls.

What Apple announced today with the new MacBook Pro with touch and OLED feels like an obvious product designed for a generation of users that grew up with iPads and are now ready to graduate to a Mac for more intensive workflows. It also seems designed for people like me, who have gotten so familiar with the hybrid interactions of a modular iPad Pro and have found the Mac’s strict trackpad-only affair to be too limiting. Since I started using my MacBook Pro more earlier this year because of coding agents and AI apps, I can’t tell you how many times I’ve instinctively reached out to touch the screen, only to remember that, unlike with an iPad Pro, I can’t.

Based on my brief hands-on time with the new MacBook Pro today, it feels like Apple delivered pretty much what I expected. Which is to say: they brought multitouch to the Mac, and optimized the macOS UI for it in the process, without turning the Mac into an iPad or fundamentally altering the nature of a MacBook Pro. It’s the laptop we know, with a (much) better display and lighter footprint because of OLED, now with a secondary input method that is optional and consistent with the work we’ve seen from the company on iPadOS.

If you’ve ever used an iPad Pro, you should feel right at home with the new MacBook Pro. If the Dock is hidden, you can swipe up from the bottom edge of the display to show it and tap on an app icon to open it. You can scroll any list of items by swiping; swipe up with four fingers to summon Mission Control and switch between spaces; long-press a document in Finder to initiate drag and drop. As you perform all these actions on the new MacBook Pro, you’ll notice that Apple did a few things to optimize and fine-tune the experience, which I asked about immediately during my hands-on time at Apple’s “experience” today.

When macOS detects touch input, it automatically spaces out certain UI elements to give them more room to breathe and, therefore, larger touch targets that are easier to sloppily operate with your fingers. In contextual menus, for instance, the distance between menu items in a list grows larger:

The same menu activated via the trackpad (left) has a denser list compared to touch activation (right).

When you long-press a file in Finder, the item swiftly “lifts up” under your finger to signify that it’s been selected – a UX detail that is typically seen on iOS and iPadOS. At this point, you can either drag the item away and drop it somewhere else, or you can let go, and the resulting contextual menu will be, once again, more spaced out than when activated via the regular pointer:

The selected item lifts on-screen when long-pressing in Finder (left) and the context menu is more spaced out when activated via touch (right).

In my brief hands-on time with the product (fun detail: three hours after the introduction, all machines were already removed from the hands-on tables), it became apparent that Apple did a lot of work to ensure that touch optimizations are everywhere in macOS Golden Gate. The implementation of touch in a historically not-touch-friendly OS has happened in a variety of ways. For starters, all system apps support touch input because, by default, macOS does the heavy lifting to translate touch input to cursor input. This also means that, regardless of which app you download and whether it’s been optimized for touch on macOS or not, basic touch interactions are going to be supported, even if the app is old and not optimized for the new MacBook Pro yet. I haven’t seen this in action myself, but my understanding is that every app is going to just work out of the box.

Second, developers can specifically optimize their apps’ UIs for touch if they so choose. Apple has already published some developer videos about bringing touch to the Mac, and more resources are coming soon alongside Xcode 27.3. From what I’ve seen today, the optimizations that developers can bring to their apps for touch seem fairly extensive. For example, I’ve seen a custom color picker in DaVinci Resolve (which worked with Apple on this ahead of time) as well as a custom slider that appeared when the user’s finger was hovering over that UI element. I’m curious to know about the extent to which developers can customize their UIs for touch, and if landing on hybrid iPad-Mac UI conventions will become the norm for multi-platform apps.

Third, there is no Apple Pencil support on the Mac yet (although everyone here is asking Apple PR reps the same questions about it over and over), and it’s possible to turn off touch input altogether under Accessibility. If you’re interested in buying an OLED MacBook just for the display (which does look extremely good in person and puts the Tandem OLED panels previously seen on some Lenovo laptops to shame) and don’t want to ever touch the display, that setting is for you. Also seen in Accessibility, and turned off by default: there’s a preference to enable Display Zoom, which will let you pinch to zoom into any part of the macOS UI to make it larger and easier to read.

I haven’t spent a lot of time testing the new MacBook Pro; I’m sure I’ll have more thoughts and questions about it when I get to actually try one and use it for regular work tasks. But here’s what I think so far:

I think too many people ascribe too much importance to something that Steve Jobs said 16 years ago without realizing that so many things in our society have changed since.

That famous quote from 2010 comes from a time before Apple even knew that the iPad was going to be a massive success. That quote predates an entire generation of kids who have grown up using iPads, are now familiar with multitouch, and probably think that it’s odd that MacBooks only come with a tiny trackpad and no direct manipulation. That quote belongs to a time when iPhones had only existed for three years; 16 years later, touchscreens have penetrated every corner of the tech consumer market, from gaming consoles and car dashboards to smart fridges and coffee makers.

I’d argue that the Mac’s lack of touch is a liability at this point. Its omission has turned from a deliberate design decision that made sense for its time to a choice dictated by inertia and, perhaps, an unwillingness to challenge the status quo. Which is especially funny since the “status quo” of Apple is that of a company that sells millions of touch-enabled devices every year and considerably fewer trackpad-only ones. The lack of touch on the Mac feels like a self-inflicted problem that has no reason to exist anymore, and which John Ternus is rightfully rectifying for the modern age.

As someone who has spent the past decade working on an iPad, and is now increasingly shifting his workflow to the Mac, I think it’s great that we’re getting touch as an option on the Mac. I’ve always been in favor of hardware that can adapt to the user instead of the other way around.

The MacBook Pro getting touch support feels like another step in the long arc of Apple meeting users where they are – even if it means “contradicting” a quote from 2010. We’re moving on, and it’s about time.

news.original_content:
Ever since I got my hands on the very first iPad Pro all the way back in November 2015, I’ve gotten used to a certain type of computer interaction that Steve Jobs once decried as “ergonomically terrible”: working with a keyboard, but sometimes also touching the screen. Of course, that interaction became even more common when Apple introduced the Magic Keyboard with trackpad for iPad Pro in 2020: by that point, I was fully alternating between trackpad control and direct touch input on a tablet that allowed me to “rip off” the display and walk away with it whenever I wanted.

Steve Jobs was right about many things, but I’ve long disagreed with his take on the “terrible” ergonomics of touchscreen laptops. Sure, you don’t want to be forced to interact with a laptop display that sits perpendicular to the keyboard at all times. But for the occasional interaction that benefits from direct manipulation of content – whether that’s zooming on a picture or rotating a 3D object or game character with your fingers – it’s nice to have a secondary input method that does not rely on a UX abstraction such as a trackpad. Think of it as motion controls on a Nintendo Switch: you primarily play games with a controller and physical buttons, but, sometimes, it is nicer – and easier – to rely on the gyroscope for motion controls.

What Apple announced today with the new MacBook Pro with touch and OLED feels like an obvious product designed for a generation of users that grew up with iPads and are now ready to graduate to a Mac for more intensive workflows. It also seems designed for people like me, who have gotten so familiar with the hybrid interactions of a modular iPad Pro and have found the Mac’s strict trackpad-only affair to be too limiting. Since I started using my MacBook Pro more earlier this year because of coding agents and AI apps, I can’t tell you how many times I’ve instinctively reached out to touch the screen, only to remember that, unlike with an iPad Pro, I can’t.

Based on my brief hands-on time with the new MacBook Pro today, it feels like Apple delivered pretty much what I expected. Which is to say: they brought multitouch to the Mac, and optimized the macOS UI for it in the process, without turning the Mac into an iPad or fundamentally altering the nature of a MacBook Pro. It’s the laptop we know, with a (much) better display and lighter footprint because of OLED, now with a secondary input method that is optional and consistent with the work we’ve seen from the company on iPadOS.

If you’ve ever used an iPad Pro, you should feel right at home with the new MacBook Pro. If the Dock is hidden, you can swipe up from the bottom edge of the display to show it and tap on an app icon to open it. You can scroll any list of items by swiping; swipe up with four fingers to summon Mission Control and switch between spaces; long-press a document in Finder to initiate drag and drop. As you perform all these actions on the new MacBook Pro, you’ll notice that Apple did a few things to optimize and fine-tune the experience, which I asked about immediately during my hands-on time at Apple’s “experience” today.

When macOS detects touch input, it automatically spaces out certain UI elements to give them more room to breathe and, therefore, larger touch targets that are easier to sloppily operate with your fingers. In contextual menus, for instance, the distance between menu items in a list grows larger:

The same menu activated via the trackpad (left) has a denser list compared to touch activation (right).

When you long-press a file in Finder, the item swiftly “lifts up” under your finger to signify that it’s been selected – a UX detail that is typically seen on iOS and iPadOS. At this point, you can either drag the item away and drop it somewhere else, or you can let go, and the resulting contextual menu will be, once again, more spaced out than when activated via the regular pointer:

The selected item lifts on-screen when long-pressing in Finder (left) and the context menu is more spaced out when activated via touch (right).

In my brief hands-on time with the product (fun detail: three hours after the introduction, all machines were already removed from the hands-on tables), it became apparent that Apple did a lot of work to ensure that touch optimizations are everywhere in macOS Golden Gate. The implementation of touch in a historically not-touch-friendly OS has happened in a variety of ways. For starters, all system apps support touch input because, by default, macOS does the heavy lifting to translate touch input to cursor input. This also means that, regardless of which app you download and whether it’s been optimized for touch on macOS or not, basic touch interactions are going to be supported, even if the app is old and not optimized for the new MacBook Pro yet. I haven’t seen this in action myself, but my understanding is that every app is going to just work out of the box.

Second, developers can specifically optimize their apps’ UIs for touch if they so choose. Apple has already published some developer videos about bringing touch to the Mac, and more resources are coming soon alongside Xcode 27.3. From what I’ve seen today, the optimizations that developers can bring to their apps for touch seem fairly extensive. For example, I’ve seen a custom color picker in DaVinci Resolve (which worked with Apple on this ahead of time) as well as a custom slider that appeared when the user’s finger was hovering over that UI element. I’m curious to know about the extent to which developers can customize their UIs for touch, and if landing on hybrid iPad-Mac UI conventions will become the norm for multi-platform apps.

Third, there is no Apple Pencil support on the Mac yet (although everyone here is asking Apple PR reps the same questions about it over and over), and it’s possible to turn off touch input altogether under Accessibility. If you’re interested in buying an OLED MacBook just for the display (which does look extremely good in person and puts the Tandem OLED panels previously seen on some Lenovo laptops to shame) and don’t want to ever touch the display, that setting is for you. Also seen in Accessibility, and turned off by default: there’s a preference to enable Display Zoom, which will let you pinch to zoom into any part of the macOS UI to make it larger and easier to read.

I haven’t spent a lot of time testing the new MacBook Pro; I’m sure I’ll have more thoughts and questions about it when I get to actually try one and use it for regular work tasks. But here’s what I think so far:

I think too many people ascribe too much importance to something that Steve Jobs said 16 years ago without realizing that so many things in our society have changed since.

That famous quote from 2010 comes from a time before Apple even knew that the iPad was going to be a massive success. That quote predates an entire generation of kids who have grown up using iPads, are now familiar with multitouch, and probably think that it’s odd that MacBooks only come with a tiny trackpad and no direct manipulation. That quote belongs to a time when iPhones had only existed for three years; 16 years later, touchscreens have penetrated every corner of the tech consumer market, from gaming consoles and car dashboards to smart fridges and coffee makers.

I’d argue that the Mac’s lack of touch is a liability at this point. Its omission has turned from a deliberate design decision that made sense for its time to a choice dictated by inertia and, perhaps, an unwillingness to challenge the status quo. Which is especially funny since the “status quo” of Apple is that of a company that sells millions of touch-enabled devices every year and considerably fewer trackpad-only ones. The lack of touch on the Mac feels like a self-inflicted problem that has no reason to exist anymore, and which John Ternus is rightfully rectifying for the modern age.

As someone who has spent the past decade working on an iPad, and is now increasingly shifting his workflow to the Mac, I think it’s great that we’re getting touch as an option on the Mac. I’ve always been in favor of hardware that can adapt to the user instead of the other way around.

news.article_content_zh:
自从我在 2015 年 11 月拿到第一台 iPad Pro 以来，我就已经习惯了史蒂夫·乔布斯曾经斥责为“不符合人体工程学”的某种类型的计算机交互：使用键盘，但有时也触摸屏幕。当然，当苹果在 2020 年为 iPad Pro 推出带触控板的妙控键盘时，这种交互变得更加普遍：到那时，我在平板电脑上完全在触控板控制和直接触摸输入之间切换，这让我可以“撕掉”显示屏，并在我想要的时候带走它。

史蒂夫·乔布斯在很多事情上都是正确的，但我长期以来一直不同意他对触摸屏笔记本电脑“糟糕”的人体工程学的看法。当然，您不想被迫始终与垂直于键盘的笔记本电脑显示屏进行交互。但对于偶尔受益于直接操作内容的交互（无论是缩放图片还是用手指旋转 3D 对象或游戏角色），最好有一个不依赖于 UX 抽象（例如触控板）的辅助输入方法。将其视为 Nintendo Switch 上的运动控制：您主要使用控制器和物理按钮玩游戏，但有时，依靠陀螺仪进行运动控制会更好且更容易。

Apple 今天推出的带有触摸屏和 OLED 功能的新款 MacBook Pro 显然是一款专为伴随 iPad 长大、现在准备升级到 Mac 进行更密集工作流程的一代用户而设计的产品。它似乎也是为像我这样的人设计的，我已经非常熟悉模块化 iPad Pro 的混合交互，并且发现 Mac 严格的仅限触控板的功能过于有限。自从今年早些时候因为编码代理和人工智能应用程序而开始更多地使用 MacBook Pro 以来，我无法告诉你有多少次我本能地伸手触摸屏幕，结果却记住，与 iPad Pro 不同，我不能。

根据我今天短暂试用新款 MacBook Pro 的时间，感觉苹果几乎满足了我的预期。也就是说：他们为 Mac 带来了多点触控，并在此过程中为其优化了 macOS UI，而没有将 Mac 变成 iPad，也没有从根本上改变 MacBook Pro 的本质。这是我们所知道的笔记本电脑，由于采用了 OLED，因此具有更好的显示屏和更轻的占地面积，现在还具有可选的辅助输入法，并且与我们在 iPadOS 上看到的该公司的工作一致。

如果您曾经使用过 iPad Pro，那么新款 MacBook Pro 应该会给您带来宾至如归的感觉。如果 Dock 被隐藏，您可以从显示屏的底部边缘向上滑动以显示它，然后点击应用程序图标将其打开。您可以通过滑动来滚动任何项目列表；四指向上滑动即可召唤任务控制中心并在空间之间切换；长按 Finder 中的文档即可启动拖放。当你在新款 MacBook Pro 上执行所有这些操作时，你会注意到苹果做了一些事情来优化和微调体验，我在今天的苹果“体验”体验中立即询问了这些问题。

当 macOS 检测到触摸输入时，它会自动间隔开某些 UI 元素，以便为它们提供更多的呼吸空间，因此，更大的触摸目标更容易用手指进行操作。例如，在上下文菜单中，列表中菜单项之间的距离会变大：

与触摸激活（右）相比，通过触控板激活的相同菜单（左）具有更密集的列表。

当您长按 Finder 中的某个文件时，该项目会在您的手指下迅速“抬起”，表示它已被选中 - 这是 iOS 和 iPadOS 上常见的 UX 细节。此时，您可以将项目拖走并将其放在其他位置，也可以放开，生成的上下文菜单将再次比通过常规指针激活时间隔更大：

在 Finder 中长按时，所选项目会在屏幕上浮起（左），而通过触摸激活时，上下文菜单的间距会更大（右）。

在我短暂的产品实践过程中（有趣的细节：介绍后三个小时，所有机器都已从实践台上移走），很明显，Apple 做了很多工作来确保 macOS Golden Gate 中的触摸优化无处不在。在历史上不支持触摸的操作系统中，触摸的实现有多种方式。对于初学者来说，所有系统应用程序都支持触摸输入，因为默认情况下，macOS 会承担将触摸输入转换为光标输入的繁重工作。这也意味着，无论您下载哪个应用程序，也无论它是否针对 macOS 上的触摸进行了优化，都将支持基本的触摸交互，即使该应用程序很旧并且尚未针对新 MacBook Pro 进行优化。我自己还没有看到过这种情况，但我的理解是每个应用程序都可以开箱即用。

其次，如果开发者愿意的话，他们可以专门优化应用程序的触摸用户界面。 Apple 已经发布了一些有关为 Mac 带来触控功能的开发者视频，更多资源很快就会与 Xcode 27.3 一起发布。从我今天所看到的来看，开发人员可以为其应用程序带来的触摸优化似乎相当广泛。例如，我在 DaVinci Resolve 中看到了一个自定义颜色选择器（它提前与 Apple 合作），以及当用户的手指悬停在该 UI 元素上时出现的自定义滑块。我很想知道开发人员可以在多大程度上自定义触摸 UI，以及 iPad-Mac 混合 UI 约定是否会成为多平台应用程序的常态。

第三，Mac 上尚不支持 Apple Pencil（尽管这里的每个人都一遍又一遍地向 Apple 公关代表询问相同的问题），并且可以在“辅助功能”下完全关闭触摸输入。如果你有兴趣购买 OLED MacBook 只是为了显示屏（它看起来确实非常好，并且让以前在一些联想笔记本电脑上看到的串联 OLED 面板相形见绌）并且不想触摸显示屏，那么该设置适合你。也可以在辅助功能中看到，默认情况下关闭：有一个启用“显示缩放”的首选项，这将允许您捏合放大 macOS UI 的任何部分，使其更大且更易于阅读。

我没有花很多时间测试新款 MacBook Pro；我确信当我真正尝试并将其用于日常工作任务时，我会对它有更多的想法和问题。但到目前为止我的想法是：

我认为太多人过于重视史蒂夫·乔布斯 16 年前所说的话，却没有意识到我们社会中的许多事情已经发生了变化。

这句 2010 年的名言出自苹果公司甚至不知道 iPad 将取得巨大成功之前。这句话出现的时间早于使用 iPad 长大的整整一代孩子，他们现在已经熟悉了多点触控，并且可能认为 MacBook 只配备了一个很小的触控板并且没有直接操控功能，这很奇怪。这句话发生在 iPhone 才问世三年的时代。 16 年后，触摸屏已经渗透到科技消费市场的各个角落，从游戏机和汽车仪表板到智能冰箱和咖啡机。

我认为 Mac 缺乏触控功能在这一点上是一个缺点。它的遗漏已经从一个在当时有意义的深思熟虑的设计决定变成了一种由惯性决定的选择，也许是不愿意挑战现状。这尤其有趣，因为苹果公司的“现状”是一家每年销售数百万台触控设备的公司，而纯触控设备的数量要少得多。 Mac 上缺乏触摸感觉就像是一个自己造成的问题，没有理由再存在了，而 John Ternus 正在为现代纠正这个问题。

作为一个在过去十年中一直在 iPad 上工作的人，现在越来越多地将工作流程转移到 Mac，我认为我们在 Mac 上获得触摸作为一个选项真是太好了。我一直赞成能够适应用户的硬件，而不是相反。

MacBook Pro 获得触摸支持感觉就像是苹果满足用户需求的漫长弧线中的又一步——即使这意味着与 2010 年的一句话“矛盾”。我们正在继续前进，而且是时候了。

news.author: Bloomberg
news.original_content:
Mark Bergen / Bloomberg:
A profile of Nscale CEO Josh Payne, who is proceeding with plans for a US IPO that sources say, is targeting a $30B valuation despite some investor pushback  —  Sheryl Sandberg says the 32-year-old executive reminds her of Mark Zuckerberg.
news.content_snippet: Sheryl Sandberg says the 32-year-old executive reminds her of Mark Zuckerberg. Josh Payne must now take his startup public at a tumultuous moment for the AI industry.
news.summary_en: Nscale CEO Josh Payne is forging ahead with plans for a U.S. IPO targeting a massive $30 billion valuation, despite mounting pushback from skeptical investors. Backed by high-profile endorsements comparing the 32-year-old executive to Mark Zuckerberg, the startup is aggressively capitalizing on the AI compute infrastructure frenzy before the market window narrows.

news.summary_zh: 算力基础设施公司首席执行官顶住投资人质疑，坚持推进300亿美元估值的赴美上市计划

news.summary_en: OpenAI unveiled its layered defense architecture designed to detect frontier model misalignment and unauthorized agent maneuvers during runtime. news.original_content: Ropes & Gray is developing AI for transactional diligence with OpenAI. Lawyers review grouped documents, summaries, and reports before advising clients.
news.content_snippet: Ropes & Gray is developing AI for transactional diligence with OpenAI. Lawyers review grouped documents, summaries, and reports before advising clients.
news.summary_en: Global law firm Ropes & Gray has integrated OpenAI technology to streamline transactional due diligence. Lawyers leverage the tool to automatically categorize documents, generate summaries, and compile reports, significantly accelerating their advisory workflows.
news.title_zh: 顶级律所联手OpenAI重塑尽职调查
news.summary_zh: 老牌律所Ropes & Gray深度接入OpenAI大模型，通过AI自动化归档与摘要分析，大幅压缩尽职调查的案头时间
news.article_content_zh:
Ropes & Gray正在将其交易尽职调查业务进行数字化转型。通过将OpenAI的模型集成至法律工作流中，该公司能够对海量的交易文件进行快速聚类分析。

在实际应用中，律师不再需要从零开始阅读每一份文档。AI系统会先行介入，对文档进行自动分类并生成关键事实摘要，律师则在审核这些AI产出的报告后再为客户提供最终建议。这一举措标志着高端法律咨询行业正逐步摆脱纯人力的模式，转向人机协同的新范式。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 法律巨头Ropes & Gray正式引入OpenAI技术栈，旨在处理海量交易文件的尽职调查流程。律师通过AI对各类法律文档进行自动归档、提取核心摘要与智能报告撰写，以此辅助高压下的律师决策。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Global law firm Ropes & Gray has integrated OpenAI technology to streamline transactional due diligence. Lawyers leverage the tool to automatically categorize documents, generate summaries, and compile reports, significantly accelerating their advisory workflows.

elements_zh.why: 降低法律流程中繁琐的人力成本，提升复杂并购项目的交付效率

elements_en.what: Automated document clustering, summarizing, and report generation via OpenAI
elements_en.why: To reduce manual labor and accelerate high-stakes M&A workflows

ai_analysis.insight_en: Law firms finally realized it's better to let AI parse thousands of pages of mind-numbing contracts than to burn out junior associates. AI does the heavy lifting while lawyers keep the liability—it's a match made in corporate heaven.

news.title: How Maynard v. Snapchat, a 2016 lawsuit linked to a car crash involving Snapchat's speed filter, sparked social media's legal reckoning over user safety (Olivia Carville/Bloomberg)
news.title_en: How Maynard v. Snapchat, a 2016 lawsuit linked to a car crash involving Snapchat's speed filter, sparked social media's legal reckoning over user safety (Olivia Carville/Bloomberg)
news.author: Bloomberg
news.original_content:
Olivia Carville / Bloomberg:
How Maynard v. Snapchat, a 2016 lawsuit linked to a car crash involving Snapchat's speed filter, sparked social media's legal reckoning over user safety  —  The rain had only just let up when the night shift ended at the Bay Breeze Sea
news.content_snippet: The rain had only just let up when the night shift ended at the Bay Breeze Seafood Restaurant in Lovejoy, Georgia.
news.summary_en: A landmark lawsuit over a catastrophic car crash spurred by Snapchat's speed filter has successfully pierced the industry's Section 230 liability shield, ruling that negligent product design is actionable. The case established that app features incentivizing reckless behavior hold tech companies liable as product manufacturers. This legal precedent has triggered a nationwide reckoning, paving the way for hundreds of current suits holding social giants accountable for algorithm-driven harm.
news.title_zh: 测速滤镜车祸案成转折点，社交平台产品缺陷责任清算拉开序幕
news.summary_zh: 八年前因Snapchat测速滤镜诱发严重车祸的诉讼，打破了社交平台免责神话并引发行业监管海啸

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 在持续数年的司法拉锯中，针对Snapchat测速滤镜诱发时速超百英里车祸的诉讼案件取得关键突破，法院认定其功能设计具有诱导危险行为的缺陷。原告受害方以产品设计缺陷为由突破了科技行业赖以自保的《通信规范法》第230条免责屏障。这一判例彻底改写了硅谷的司法防御策略，直接引发了全美各地数百起针对社交平台算法成瘾、致使青少年心理或人身伤害的集体诉讼。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: A landmark lawsuit over a catastrophic car crash spurred by Snapchat's speed filter has successfully pierced the industry's Section 230 liability shield, ruling that negligent product design is actionable. The case established that app features incentivizing reckless behavior hold tech companies liable as product manufacturers. This legal precedent has triggered a nationwide reckoning, paving the way for hundreds of current suits holding social giants accountable for algorithm-driven harm.

elements_zh.where: 美国各级法院与司法诉讼程序中
elements_zh.what: 法院突破第230条保护伞，裁定社交软件的功能设计缺陷需承担产品侵权责任
elements_zh.why: 平台为争夺注意力推出将真实危险游戏化的滤镜功能，直接导致严重交通事故并危及公共安全

elements_en.who: Snap Inc. and crash victim plaintiffs
elements_en.what: Courts pierced the Section 230 shield by ruling negligent product design actionable under tort law
elements_en.why: Platform gamified reckless driving for user engagement, directly resulting in catastrophic bodily harm

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 过去硅谷巨头总把第230条当免死金牌，产品怎么诱人作死就怎么做，出了事一律推脱是用户自己的问题。测速滤镜这记司法耳光终于把法官打醒了：把产品功能做成‘催命符’换取用户停留时长，就别妄想继续在法庭上装人畜无害的中立管道。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Big Tech treated Section 230 as an omnipotent get-out-of-jail-free card for years, gamifying reckless behavior for engagement while blaming users when disasters struck. This ruling finally demolished that facade: if you design app features that effectively incentivize lethal stupidity, you are a negligent product maker, not an innocent utility pipe.

news.title: STMicro reports Q3 revenue up 17.9% YoY to $3.76B, operating income up 98% YoY to $429M, vs. $400.5M est., and forecasts $4.15B in Q4 revenue, vs. $4.10B est. (Reuters)
news.title_en: STMicro reports Q3 revenue up 17.9% YoY to $3.76B, operating income up 98% YoY to $429M, vs. $400.5M est., and forecasts $4.15B in Q4 revenue, vs. $4.10B est. (Reuters)
news.author: Reuters
news.original_content:
Reuters:
STMicro reports Q3 revenue up 17.9% YoY to $3.76B, operating income up 98% YoY to $429M, vs. $400.5M est., and forecasts $4.15B in Q4 revenue, vs. $4.10B est.  —  STMicroelectronics (STMPA.PA) reported a third-quarter operating profit above market expecta
news.content_snippet: STMicroelectronics (STMPA.PA) reported a third-quarter operating profit above market expectations on Thursday …
news.summary_en: European chipmaker STMicroelectronics posted robust third-quarter financial results, reporting a 17.9% YoY revenue increase to $3.76 billion and a 98% surge in operating income to $429 million, handily beating market expectations. Driven by resilient demand across automotive and industrial sectors, the company also projected Q4 revenue of $4.15 billion, topping analyst estimates of $4.10 billion.

news.summary_zh: 意法半导体第三季度营业利润同比暴增98%至4.29亿美元，第四季度营收指引同样高于市场预期

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 欧洲芯片巨头意法半导体在最新公布的第三季度财报中交出亮眼成绩单，当季营收同比增长17.9%达到37.6亿美元，营业利润更是同比激增98%至4.29亿美元，双双突破华尔街普遍预期。得益于汽车与工业领域芯片需求的稳固支撑，公司同时给出了41.5亿美元的第四季度强劲营收指引，再次击败市场普遍预估的41亿美元。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: European chipmaker STMicroelectronics posted robust third-quarter financial results, reporting a 17.9% YoY revenue increase to $3.76 billion and a 98% surge in operating income to $429 million, handily beating market expectations. Driven by resilient demand across automotive and industrial sectors, the company also projected Q4 revenue of $4.15 billion, topping analyst estimates of $4.10 billion.
