items.title: Meta quietly launches Style Sketch, an AI fashion app that helps users put together outfit ideas using clothes they own, in Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand (Aisha Malik/TechCrunch)
items.title_en: Meta quietly launches Style Sketch, an AI fashion app that helps users put together outfit ideas using clothes they own, in Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand (Aisha Malik/TechCrunch)
items.author: TechCrunch
items.article_content:
Meta has quietly launched Style Sketch, an AI fashion app that helps users put together outfit ideas using clothes they already own. The app connects to Instagram to build a virtual closet from photos you’ve posted, or lets you add items manually by snapping a photo, recording a quick video, or uploading images from your camera roll.

Style Sketch then suggests outfit combinations built from your wardrobe matched to your style. Users can then try on the outfits on a “realistic model matched to your body shape and skin tone,” the app description reads.

The app, which was first spotted by social media consultant Matt Navarra, is available in Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand on iOS and Android.

Meta did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment. It’s unknown whether Meta plans to launch Style Sketch more widely.

🚨 Meta quietly launched an AI fashion app! 👗Style Sketch connects to Facebook & Instagram to build a wardrobe from photos you’ve already posted• 👕 AI outfits from clothes you own• 🪞 Virtual try-ons matched to your body• ☀️ Weather-based looks• ✈️ Trip packing plans pic.twitter.com/uNYX6VHRCn

Several apps already use AI to help users digitize their wardrobes and visualize new outfits, including startups like Alta. Even Google Photos offers tools that let users turn photos of their clothes into digital closets where they can create new outfit ideas.

To compete with what’s already on the market, Meta will likely rely less on the novelty of the idea and more on the app’s integration with Instagram, where users already have a visual record of their personal style.

Rather than relying on random suggestions, users can also select a specific item from their wardrobe and get fresh outfit ideas built around it, according to the app description.

The app can also help users plan outfits for trips. If they enter their destination, trip length, and planned activities, users can get a day-by-day outfit plan that takes the weather forecast and itinerary into account.

Style Sketch is one of many AI apps from Meta in recent months. Most recently, the company launched an app called Waddle World, which essentially looks like a Tamagotchi clone, but with AI. Meta has also launched Pocket, a tool for vibe-coding games, and Vibes, which lets users quickly generate AI-powered videos.

The wave of new apps is part of a broader effort at Meta to release more apps. The Wall Street Journal reported earlier this year that CEO Mark Zuckerberg told employees the company plans to release far more apps than it has historically, as AI-driven efficiencies have made it faster and easier to ship new apps.

items.title: On Amazon's earnings call, Andy Jassy says outside AI shopping agents are "still not great, nor more convenient than coming to a retailer directly" (Sebastian Herrera/Fortune)
items.title_en: On Amazon's earnings call, Andy Jassy says outside AI shopping agents are "still not great, nor more convenient than coming to a retailer directly" (Sebastian Herrera/Fortune)
items.author: Fortune
items.article_content:
Amazon Chief Executive Andy Jassy told investors Thursday not to worry about bots invading its online store and rendering it useless.

Jassy’s comments, made during a call with analysts following the company’s quarterly earnings report, came about a month after the e-commerce giant blocked Meta Platforms’ popular new AI assistant, Muse, from accessing its online store. Amazon said in September that Muse’s access would violate the conditions of use its customers have agreed to.

While not naming Muse, Jassy said few customers are buying with outside shopping agents because the experience is “still not great, nor more convenient than coming to a retailer directly.”

Amazon also has its own shopping agent, “Alexa for shopping,” that it is eager for customers to use.

During the analyst call, Jassy said more than 400 million customers have used Alexa for shopping in the last year, with “customer interactions” growing 570% year over year. He also said that U.S. customers using its shopping agent spend 50% more per order than those who do not use it.

Meta, meanwhile, has seen huge growth for Muse. The AI agent quickly unseated ChatGPT as the top free app on Apple’s App Store, and Meta Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg said last week that more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had already set up the Muse assistant since it was released in early September.

The app can plug into calendars, emails, and other phone functions to run tasks autonomously on behalf of users. It is one of several personal assistants that tech companies such as OpenAI have been rolling out in recent months.

Zuckerberg said the most common use case for Muse has been shopping, with more than a quarter of the people using the agent engaging in shopping and the average purchase size topping $200.

“Obviously, not everyone wants to be an early adopter. That’s fine,” Zuckerberg said. “We’ll work with folks on the terms that makes sense for them.”

items.article_content_zh:
亚马逊首席执行官安迪·贾西周四告诉投资者，不要担心机器人入侵其在线商店并使其变得毫无用处。

Jassy 在该公司季度收益报告后与分析师的电话会议上发表了上述言论，大约一个月前，这家电子商务巨头阻止了 Meta Platforms 广受欢迎的新人工智能助手 Muse 访问其在线商店。亚马逊去年 9 月表示，Muse 的访问将违反其客户同意的使用条件。

虽然没有透露 Muse 的名字，但 Jassy 表示，很少有顾客通过外部代购机构购买商品，因为这种体验“仍然不是很好，也比直接到零售商那里更方便”。

亚马逊还拥有自己的购物代理“Alexa for Shopping”，渴望客户使用。

Jassy 在分析师电话会议上表示，去年有超过 4 亿客户使用 Alexa 进行购物，“客户互动”同比增长 570%。他还表示，使用其代购的美国顾客每笔订单的花费比不使用代购的顾客高出 50%。

与此同时，Meta 也见证了 Muse 的巨大增长。这款人工智能代理迅速取代 ChatGPT 成为苹果应用商店中排名第一的免费应用程序，Meta 首席执行官马克扎克伯格上周表示，自 9 月初发布以来，美国和加拿大已有超过 1000 万人安装了 Muse 助手。

该应用程序可以插入日历、电子邮件和其他电话功能，以代表用户自主运行任务。它是 OpenAI 等科技公司近几个月推出的几款个人助理之一。

扎克伯格表示，Muse 最常见的用例是购物，超过四分之一的人使用该代理进行购物，平均购买金额超过 200 美元。

“显然，并不是每个人都想成为早期采用者。这很好，”扎克伯格说。 “我们将按照对他们有意义的条款与人们合作。”

items.title: Sandisk reports Q1 revenue up 378% YoY to $11B, vs. $10.7B est., forecasts Q2 revenue above est., announces an 8-for-1 stock split; SNDK drops 4%+ after hours (MarketWatch)
items.title_en: Sandisk reports Q1 revenue up 378% YoY to $11B, vs. $10.7B est., forecasts Q2 revenue above est., announces an 8-for-1 stock split; SNDK drops 4%+ after hours (MarketWatch)
items.author: MarketWatch
items.article_content:
Less than two years after it became an independent company again, Sandisk plans to conduct a stock split.

Shares are up more than 2,600% since the company separated from Western Digital (WDC) in February 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data. They've become one of the highest-priced components in the S&P 500 SPX, finishing Thursday at $1,330. Just five companies in the index had higher stock prices than that as of the close.

A high stock price in isolation doesn't mean much, especially in an era when investors can easily trade fractional shares. That said, stock splits lower the price by creating more shares that are each worth commensurately less, and companies tend to say that the move makes the shares more accessible to investors.

Sandisk (SNDK) was no exception as it announced an eight-for-one stock split to be effective on Nov. 19. The company noted that the lower stock price could help make shares more accessible to employees purchasing them through plans.

A stock split doesn't change the overall value of a company or what each investor owns. Research is mixed on whether stock splits deliver the intended benefits of making shares more appealing to retail investors, though some experts have said there's a psychological advantage to having a somewhat lower price that doesn't seem so daunting.

The announcement came in conjunction with Sandisk's earnings report, in which it gave a revenue forecast that calls for $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion during the December quarter. Analysts tracked by FactSet had been looking for $12.3 billion.

Revenue for the September quarter came in at $11 billion, up 378% from a year prior, while analysts were modeling $10.7 billion.

CEO David Goeckeler called out "robust and growing demand for our products," which fueled "outpaced growth in our data-center business."

Shares were down 2% in choppy trading in Thursday's extended session.

Sandisk has been a major beneficiary of the AI boom, which has fueled unprecedented demand for products that store and move data. The company has been able to grow quite profitably, as tight supply of its storage offerings has allowed it to raise prices dramatically.

To that end, the company logged an 85.1% adjusted gross margin for the September quarter, with that measure showing the portion of money Sandisk was able to retain after covering the costs of making its products. This marked an expansion from the 84.6% adjusted operating margin recorded in the June quarter.

Sandisk's forecast calls for an adjusted gross margin of 84.5% to 85.5% in the December quarter.

Adjusted earnings per share in the September quarter ballooned 6,913% to $52.60 and exceeded expectations for $46.67, although the company flagged that the percentage is "not a meaningful figure."

Sandisk shares have been among the best performers in the S&P 500 this year, rising more than 450% so far in 2026, a gain second only to that of Moderna (MRNA).

items.article_content_zh:
再次成为独立公司后不到两年，Sandisk 计划进行股票分割。

根据道琼斯市场数据，自 2025 年 2 月该公司从西部数据 (WDC) 分拆以来，该公司股价已上涨超过 2,600%。它们已成为 S&P 500 SPX 中价格最高的成分股之一，周四收于 1,330 美元。该指数中只有五家公司的股价高于收盘价。

孤立地看，高股价并没有多大意义，尤其是在投资者可以轻松交易零碎股票的时代。也就是说，股票分割会产生更多的股票，而每股股票的价值相应降低，从而降低了价格，而且公司倾向于表示，此举使投资者更容易获得这些股票。

Sandisk (SNDK) 也不例外，该公司宣布将于 11 月 19 日实施一股八股的股票分割。该公司指出，较低的股价有助于让通过计划购买股票的员工更容易获得股票。

股票分割不会改变公司的整体价值或每个投资者所拥有的资产。关于股票分割是否能带来使股票对散户投资者更具吸引力的预期好处，研究结果褒贬不一，尽管一些专家表示，较低的价格具有心理优势，但似乎并不那么令人畏惧。

该公告与 Sandisk 的收益报告同时发布，该公司在该报告中预测 12 月所在季度的收入为 122 亿至 126 亿美元。 FactSet 追踪的分析师一直在寻找 123 亿美元的资金。

9 月份季度的收入为 110 亿美元，比去年同期增长 378%，而分析师预测为 107 亿美元。

首席执行官 David Goeckeler 表示“对我们产品的强劲且不断增长的需求”推动了“我们数据中心业务的增长”。

在周四的延长交易中，该股在震荡交易中下跌了 2%。

Sandisk 是人工智能热潮的主要受益者，人工智能热潮推动了对存储和移动数据产品的前所未有的需求。该公司能够实现相当可观的盈利增长，因为其存储产品供应紧张，使其能够大幅提高价格。

为此，该公司 9 月份季度的调整后毛利率为 85.1%，该指标显示 Sandisk 在支付产品制造成本后能够保留的部分资金。这标志着 6 月份季度调整后运营利润率 84.6% 的扩大。

Sandisk 预计 12 月份季度的调整后毛利率将达到 84.5% 至 85.5%。

9 月季度调整后每股收益飙升 6,913% 至 52.60 美元，超出预期的 46.67 美元，尽管该公司表示该百分比“不是一个有意义的数字”。

Sandisk 股价是今年标普 500 指数中表现最好的股票之一，2026 年迄今上涨超过 450%，涨幅仅次于 Moderna (MRNA)。

items.title: Sources: Instagram is offering select creators $50K to $500K to cross-post their long-form YouTube content to its new "Features" product (Business Insider)
items.title_en: Sources: Instagram is offering select creators $50K to $500K to cross-post their long-form YouTube content to its new "Features" product (Business Insider)
items.author: Business Insider
items.article_content:
Save Saved Listen to this story "We've been public about the fact that we are funding Features content directly with some creators right now to support them," a Meta spokesperson told Business Insider. "The details of those deals are confidential, but we're excited to see the content going live."

On Monday, Instagram unveiled an overhaul of its video formats. Most importantly, it's resurrecting IGTV — a long-form video product Instagram launched in 2018 and sunset in 2022 — in the form of Features. The horizontal, wide-screen videos will exist within the Instagram app, and can be as long as a feature film: 90 minutes.

Long-form video isn't exactly what people are used to watching on Instagram. Reels, the platform's answer to TikTok's meteoric rise, has redefined the Instagram experience and is driving time-spent and revenue across Meta's apps.

YouTube, however, reigns king as the internet's destination for sit-down, longer-form videos.

Instagram knows this. The deals do not require exclusivity to Instagram, multiple people familiar with the agreements said; one person familiar with the offers said it's asking creators to post to Instagram any of the long-form content they publish to YouTube that same day.

Reza Izad, partner at Underscore Talent, whose clients include "Subway Takes'" Kareem Rahma and Noah Beck, called the deals an "exciting opportunity" for creators.

Want more Business Insider in your news feed? Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.

"Every time there's a new feature in these apps that the company's promoting, people will have more opportunity to be seen because there's going to be algorithmic preference to this kind of content," he said. "And unlike short-form, there's not a lot of abundance."

This isn't the first time Instagram has inked paid deals with creators to lure them to post more on Meta's apps.

Last year, Meta was paying creators thousands of dollars to post short-form videos to Instagram and Facebook in the midst of TikTok's potential ban. The company has tested several bonus programs paying creators for the performance of their Reels on Instagram, though those programs have dwindled.

Back in 2021, when IGTV was still part of Instagram's big video bet, it inked deals with creators, funding long-form episodic shows from creators like TikTok's "Sway Boys" and "Dance Moms" alum Nia Sioux. Briefly, IGTV had its own monetization program, too, which let some creators earn a cut from ad revenue on the format.

While Instagram is paying some creators directly, a big question looms over the creator economy: What about the rest of them?

A major draw of YouTube is its long-standing Partner Program, which pays eligible creators a share of the ad revenue generated by their videos. Even though YouTube has increased its eligibility requirements, the potential to turn a hobby or passion project into a cash-earning career has kept YouTube on top as the go-to video platform for creators.

It's no surprise, then, that when Instagram announced its video overhaul, creators immediately had questions about monetization.

"We understand the economics matter a ton, and are exploring multiple options to help long-form creators get paid," Instagram's top executive, Adam Mosseri, wrote in an X post on Wednesday.

items.article_content_zh:
一位 Meta 发言人告诉《商业内幕》：“我们已经公开表示，我们现在正在直接向一些创作者提供资助，以支持他们的专题内容。” “这些交易的细节是保密的，但我们很高兴看到内容上线。”

周一，Instagram 公布了对其视频格式的全面改革。最重要的是，它以专题的形式复活了 IGTV——Instagram 于 2018 年推出、2022 年停用的长视频产品。横向宽屏视频将存在于 Instagram 应用程序中，长度可以与故事片一样长：90 分钟。

人们并不习惯在 Instagram 上观看长视频。 Reels 是该平台对 TikTok 迅速崛起的回应，它重新定义了 Instagram 体验，并正在推动 Meta 应用程序的时间花费和收入增长。

然而，YouTube 作为互联网上坐下来观看较长视频的目的地，占据着王者地位。

Instagram 知道这一点。多位知情人士表示，这些交易并不要求 Instagram 拥有独家经营权；一位熟悉这些优惠的人士表示，它要求创作者将他们当天在 YouTube 上发布的任何长篇内容发布到 Instagram 上。

Underscore Talent 合伙人 Reza Izad 的客户包括“Subway Takes”Kareem Rahma 和 Noah Beck，他称这些交易对创作者来说是一个“令人兴奋的机会”。

想要在新闻源中看到更多商业内幕吗？在 Google 中添加 BI，以便您在搜索重要内容时更容易找到我们的报告。

他说：“每当公司推广的这些应用程序有新功能时，人们就会有更多的机会被看到，因为算法会对此类内容产生偏好。” “与短片不同的是，它的内容并不丰富。”

这并不是 Instagram 第一次与创作者签署付费协议，以吸引他们在 Meta 的应用程序上发布更多内容。

去年，在 TikTok 可能被禁止的情况下，Meta 向创作者支付了数千美元，让他们在 Instagram 和 Facebook 上发布短片。该公司已经测试了多项奖励计划，根据 Reels 在 Instagram 上的表现向创作者支付费用，不过这些计划已经减少。

早在 2021 年，当 IGTV 仍是 Instagram 大视频赌注的一部分时，它就与创作者签署了协议，资助 TikTok 的“Sway Boys”和“Dance Moms”校友 Nia Sioux 等创作者的长篇剧集节目。简而言之，IGTV 也有自己的盈利计划，让一些创作者从该格式的广告收入中获得分成。

虽然 Instagram 直接向一些创作者付费，但创作者经济面临着一个大问题：其余的人怎么办？

YouTube的主要吸引力在于其长期的合作伙伴计划，该计划向符合条件的创作者支付其视频产生的广告收入的一部分。尽管YouTube提高了资格要求，但将爱好或激情项目转化为赚钱职业的潜力使YouTube成为创作者首选的视频平台。

因此，当 Instagram 宣布视频改革时，创作者立即对盈利产生了疑问，这也就不足为奇了。

Instagram 的首席执行官 Adam Mosseri 在周三的 X 帖子中写道：“我们非常了解经济的重要性，并且正在探索多种选择来帮助长篇创作者获得报酬。”

items.title: Amazon reports Q3 AWS revenue up 39% YoY to $45.98B, above $45.29B est., and AWS operating income up 55% to $17.77B, above $16.97B est. (Jordan Novet/CNBC)
items.title_en: Amazon reports Q3 AWS revenue up 39% YoY to $45.98B, above $45.29B est., and AWS operating income up 55% to $17.77B, above $16.97B est. (Jordan Novet/CNBC)
items.author: CNBC
items.article_content:
Amazon's cloud-computing unit reported more rapid third-quarter growth than analysts had projected.

Revenue came in at $45.98 billion, up 39% year over year and above the $45.29 billion consensus among analysts polled by StreetAccount, according to a statement. Growth in the second quarter came in at about 37%.

"Our core compute and storage revenue grew at their fastest rates in several years," Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on a conference call with analysts. The AWS growth rate was the highest since the fourth quarter of 2021.

Amazon remains the top cloud by revenue, but growth has also sped up at rivals Alphabet and Microsoft. On Wednesday Alphabet said the Google Cloud business, which contains infrastructure and Google Workspace subscriptions, more than doubled in the third quarter.

All the major clouds have been racing to build data centers that can accommodate high artificial intelligence demand. During the quarter, AWS announced plans to expand its portfolio of Nvidia graphics processing units that can handle AI workloads.

AWS also acquired data analysis startup DuckLabs and signed deals with Meta and OpenAI, according to the statement.

The AWS segment generated $17.77 billion in third-quarter operating income, up 55% and more than the $16.97 billion StreetAccount consensus.

The unit now accounts for almost 23% of Amazon's revenue, a record.

On Wednesday, Microsoft published its first earnings report that contained revenue from its Azure cloud in dollars. Azure is 72% the size of AWS, up from 58% two years ago.

AWS came before Azure and the Google Cloud Platform, with its first services appearing in 2006.

"With our continued pace of innovation, new core and AI functionality, enterprises wanting to run their core and AI workloads in AWS, and the amount of capacity that we're adding each year, we believe that AWS can grow north of 40% in each of 2027 and in 2028, and be a trillion-dollar revenue business in the next five to 10 years," Jassy said.

Google has been pumping up its cloud revenue by making its tensor processing units for AI available outside its own facilities. Now Amazon will adopt the strategy with its Trainium chips for training models, starting in late 2027.

"With Trainium demand so strong, customers continue encouraging us to make it available outside of AWS. We intend to do so late in 2027," Jassy said.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 亚马逊AWS云服务三季度实现营收459.8亿美元，同比大增39%，远超分析师预测的452.9亿美元。营收提速主要得益于核心算力和存储需求的强劲增长，以及通过扩充英伟达GPU集群并深度绑定OpenAI等AI巨头进行的资源扩张。

items.article_content_zh:
亚马逊云计算部门第三季度的增长速度超出了分析师的预期。

一份声明显示，营收为 459.8 亿美元，同比增长 39%，高于 StreetAccount 调查的分析师普遍预期的 452.9 亿美元。第二季度的增长率约为 37%。

亚马逊首席执行官安迪·贾西（Andy Jassy）在与分析师的电话会议上表示：“我们的核心计算和存储收入以几年来最快的速度增长。” AWS增长率创2021年第四季度以来最高。

按收入计算，亚马逊仍然是云计算领域的佼佼者，但竞争对手 Alphabet 和微软的增长也加快了。 Alphabet 周三表示，包括基础设施和 Google Workspace 订阅在内的谷歌云业务在第三季度增长了一倍多。

各大云都在竞相建设能够满足人工智能高需求的数据中心。本季度，AWS 宣布计划扩大其可处理人工智能工作负载的 Nvidia 图形处理单元产品组合。

声明称，AWS 还收购了数据分析初创公司 DuckLabs，并与 Meta 和 OpenAI 签署了协议。

AWS 部门第三季度营业收入为 177.7 亿美元，增长 55%，超过 StreetAccount 预期的 169.7 亿美元。

该部门目前占亚马逊收入的近 23%，创历史新高。

周三，微软发布了第一份收益报告，其中包含其 Azure 云的收入（以美元计算）。 Azure 的规模是 AWS 的 72%，高于两年前的 58%。

AWS 出现在 Azure 和 Google 云平台之前，其第一个服务于 2006 年出现。

Jassy 表示：“随着我们持续的创新步伐、新的核心和 AI 功能、希望在 AWS 中运行核心和 AI 工作负载的企业，以及我们每年增加的容量，我们相信 AWS 在 2027 年和 2028 年每年都会增长 40% 以上，并在未来 5 到 10 年内成为收入数万亿美元的业务。”

谷歌一直在通过在自己的设施之外提供人工智能张量处理单元来增加其云收入。现在，从 2027 年底开始，亚马逊将通过其用于训练模型的 Trainium 芯片采用该策略。

“由于 Trainium 需求如此强劲，客户不断鼓励我们在 AWS 之外提供它。我们打算在 2027 年晚些时候这样做，”Jassy 说。

【起因与机理】AI算力需求爆发，带动了云基础设施的资源消耗与扩张
【关键数据与实测】亚马逊AWS云服务三季度实现营收459.8亿美元，同比大增39%，远超分析师预测的452.9亿美元。
【观点态度】AI算力集群建设成核心增长点。

items.title: Reddit reports Q3 revenue up 53% YoY to $895M, vs. $878M est., DAUq up 12% to 130.3M, below est., forecasts Q4 revenue below est.; RDDT drops 17%+ after hours (Jonathan Vanian/CNBC)
items.title_en: Reddit reports Q3 revenue up 53% YoY to $895M, vs. $878M est., DAUq up 12% to 130.3M, below est., forecasts Q4 revenue below est.; RDDT drops 17%+ after hours (Jonathan Vanian/CNBC)
items.author: CNBC
items.article_content:
Reddit plans to require all users to create official accounts to access the social media platform, marking a major departure for the site known as "the front page of the internet."

The company revealed the change Thursday as part of its third-quarter earnings, in which it beat on the top and bottom lines, but provided weak fourth-quarter sales guidance. The company's shares dropped over 15% after its numbers were released.

Reddit CEO Steve Huffman told CNBC in an interview that the company's shrinking search-referral traffic from Google played a major role in its planned efforts to require people to become "logged-in" users.

A previous Google search update designed to surface "authentic" content from internet forums helped Reddit grow its user base over the past few years, but the search giant's continued push on AI overviews and related chatting features has negatively impacted referral traffic.

"I think fundamentally that relationship between Google and the rest of the internet is evolving, and so for us, this means a continued focus on our core users that come to Reddit directly," Huffman said.

Previous Google algorithm changes would "kind of come and go," Huffman said, but the company's AI efforts represent "a fundamental shift in how the Google product works, from being a traffic driver to whatever's going on now."

Huffman didn't provide any specific timing on when Reddit plans for the platform registration change, saying only that implementing it through the site would involve a lot of complexity. The company will begin testing in the fourth quarter outside of the U.S.

He said that Reddit is still determining what parts of the service logged-out users will be able to see, and will iron out the details as part of its upcoming testing.

Reddit said that daily active uniques, or DAUq, rose 12% year-over-year to 130.3 million in the third quarter, trailing Wall Street estimates of 133.7 million. U.S.-specific DAUq dropped 2% year-over-year to 50.7 million, which was below analyst projections of 53.5 million.

Huffman said that "search referral traffic is down meaningfully in this quarter" and that the trend will continue in the fourth quarter.

He said that Reddit is continuing its effort to make its platform "a daily habit" for users. "So that's where our focus is: growing those app users and logged-in users," Huffman said.

Reddit, which derives the bulk of its overall sales from online advertising, is able to monetize logged-ln users better than logged-out users, because those registered users are more active and valuable to advertisers itching to deliver more targeted ads.

"The vast majority of our revenue comes from our app users and logged-in users are direct traffic, and both of those are up Q. over Q. and so that's where our focus is," Huffman said.

The company's third-quarter sales grew 53% year-over-year, marking an end to the eight-straight quarters of revenue growth eclipsing 60% that it reported in July as part of its second-quarter earnings.

Reddit said that fourth-quarter sales will come in a range of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, which was below Wall Street estimates of $1.05 billion.

"It's still a strong guide," Huffman said about its revenue guidance. "We are still growing at an industry leading rate, and that's despite the headwinds from search referrals."

Reddit's third-quarter average revenue per user, or ARPU, came in at $6.87, which was higher than the $6.50 that analysts were expecting.

The company's "other revenue" segment, which includes its data-licensing business, jumped 35% year-over-year to $48 million in the third quarter. Reddit's two biggest data-licensing partners are OpenAI and Google.

Huffman said that Reddit remains "in negotiations" with Google over its data-licensing agreement, and said that it is "only going to do a deal that makes sense for Reddit," if it chooses to continue the partnership.

"I think there's a lot of strategic considerations that goes into that," Huffman said.

Huffman called the required registration plan a "big change" for himself, considering he "grew up on the open Internet."

"Reddit is the last platform to provide basically unfettered logged-out access, and that's largely because of me, I've been holding that line," Huffman, a Reddit co-founder, said. "I think users will probably go through the same understanding that I have, which is that it's a sign of the times. It's an evolution of how these platforms work."

Huffman later expanded on the significance of AI's impact on Reddit's user growth in an earnings call with analysts, and explained that the company plans to continue spending on marketing efforts intended to offset search-referral declines. "This is a consequential time for Reddit, and this period does remind me of about 11 years ago when I came back to the company," Huffman told analysts, referring to when he rejoined Reddit in 2015 following it's then-chief Ellen Pao stepping down. "We had a lot of conversations then about what is Reddit and what is Reddit for, and what is our place in this ecosystem. And we've been having those conversations at Reddit recently." "Reddit's mission is to create community and belonging for everyone in the world, and while there's overlap between Reddit and other players in the ecosystem, whether we're talking about social media or AI search, fundamentally, Reddit is communities and conversations," Huffman said.

WATCH: Rotations in the market are likely to continue.

items.article_content_zh:
Reddit 计划要求所有用户创建官方帐户才能访问该社交媒体平台，这标志着该网站与“互联网首页”的重大转变。

该公司周四在第三季度收益中披露了这一变化，该公司的营收和利润均超出预期，但提供了疲软的第四季度销售指引。数据公布后，该公司股价下跌超过 15%。

Reddit 首席执行官 Steve Huffman 在接受 CNBC 采访时表示，该公司来自谷歌的搜索推荐流量不断减少，在其要求人们成为“登录”用户的计划中发挥了重要作用。

谷歌之前的一次搜索更新旨在显示互联网论坛中的“真实”内容，帮助 Reddit 在过去几年中扩大了用户群，但这家搜索巨头持续推动人工智能概述和相关聊天功能，对推荐流量产生了负面影响。

“我认为从根本上来说，谷歌与互联网其他部分之间的关​​系正在不断发展，因此对我们来说，这意味着继续关注直接访问 Reddit 的核心用户，”霍夫曼说。

霍夫曼表示，谷歌之前的算法变化“有点来来去去”，但该公司的人工智能工作代表了“谷歌产品工作方式的根本性转变，从交通司机到现在发生的一切。”

霍夫曼没有提供 Reddit 计划何时进行平台注册变更的任何具体时间，只是表示通过网站实施会涉及很多复杂性。该公司将于第四季度开始在美国以外的地区进行测试。

他表示，Reddit 仍在确定注销用户能够看到该服务的哪些部分，并将在即将进行的测试中确定细节。

Reddit 表示，第三季度每日活跃独立用户数 (DAUq) 同比增长 12%，达到 1.303 亿，低于华尔街预期的 1.337 亿。美国的 DAUq 同比下降 2% 至 5070 万，低于分析师预测的 5350 万。

霍夫曼表示，“本季度搜索推荐流量大幅下降”，并且这一趋势将在第四季度继续下去。

他表示，Reddit 正在继续努力，使其平台成为用户的“日常习惯”。 “这就是我们的重点：增加应用程序用户和登录用户，”霍夫曼说。

Reddit 的大部分销售额来自在线广告，它能够比注销用户更好地通过登录用户获利，因为这些注册用户对于渴望提供更有针对性的广告的广告商来说更加活跃和有价值。

霍夫曼说：“我们的绝大多数收入来自我们的应用程序用户，而登录用户是直接流量，这两个季度都比上个季度有所增长，所以这就是我们的重点所在。”

该公司第三季度销售额同比增长 53%，结束了连续 8 个季度收入增长超过 60%（该公司 7 月份公布的第二季度收益的一部分）的情况。

Reddit 表示，第四季度销售额将在 10 亿美元至 10.3 亿美元之间，低于华尔街预期的 10.5 亿美元。

“它仍然是一个强有力的指南，”霍夫曼在谈到其收入指南时说道。 “尽管搜索推荐带来了阻力，但我们仍然以行业领先的速度增长。”

Reddit 第三季度每用户平均收入 (ARPU) 为 6.87 美元，高于分析师预期的 6.50 美元。

该公司的“其他收入”部门（包括数据许可业务）第三季度同比增长 35%，达到 4800 万美元。 Reddit 的两个最大的数据许可合作伙伴是 OpenAI 和 Google。

霍夫曼表示，Reddit 仍在与谷歌就数据许可协议进行“谈判”，并表示，如果它选择继续合作，“只会达成对 Reddit 有意义的交易”。

“我认为这其中有很多战略考虑，”霍夫曼说。

霍夫曼称所需的注册计划对他自己来说是一个“巨大的改变”，因为他“是在开放的互联网上长大的”。

Reddit 联合创始人霍夫曼表示：“Reddit 是最后一个提供基本上不受限制的注销访问的平台，这很大程度上是因为我，我一直坚持这条路线。” “我认为用户可能会和我有同样的理解，那就是这是时代的标志。这是这些平台运作方式的演变。”

随后，霍夫曼在与分析师的财报电话会议上进一步阐述了人工智能对 Reddit 用户增长影响的重要性，并解释说，该公司计划继续在营销活动上投入资金，以抵消搜索推荐量的下降。霍夫曼对分析师表示：“这对 Reddit 来说是一个重要的时刻，这段时期确实让我想起了大约 11 年前我回到公司的时候。”他指的是 2015 年 Reddit 时任首席执行官 Ellen Pao 辞职后他重新加入 Reddit 的情况。 “当时我们就什么是 Reddit、Reddit 的用途以及我们在这个生态系统中的地位进行了很多对话。最近我们一直在 Reddit 上进行这些对话。” “Reddit 的使命是为世界上的每个人创建社区和归属感，虽然 Reddit 和生态系统中的其他参与者之间存在重叠，但无论我们谈论社交媒体还是人工智能搜索，从根本上讲，Reddit 就是社区和对话，”霍夫曼说。

观察：市场的轮动可能会继续。

items.title: Intel reports Q3 revenue up 21% YoY to $16.5B, vs. $16.5B est., and forecasts Q4 revenue and adjusted EPS below estimates; INTC drops 16%+ after hours (Katie Tarasov/CNBC)
items.title_en: Intel reports Q3 revenue up 21% YoY to $16.5B, vs. $16.5B est., and forecasts Q4 revenue and adjusted EPS below estimates; INTC drops 16%+ after hours (Katie Tarasov/CNBC)
items.author: CNBC
items.article_content:
Intel shares plummeted more than 20% in extended trading on Thursday after the chipmaker issued a weak fourth-quarter forecast, citing continued softness in the global PC market.

Revenue climbed 21% from $13.7 billion a year earlier, the company said in a press release.

However, revenue in Intel's client computing and physical AI group fell 5% from the same quarter a year ago to $8.1 billion, missing estimates, even as data center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion.

Global PC shipments declined 4% in the second quarter from a year earlier due to soaring costs for memory and other components, according to Counterpoint Research.

For the current quarter, Intel said it expects adjusted earnings per share of 25 cents on revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion. Analysts were expecting revenue of $17.1 billion and EPS of 43 cents, according to LSEG.

"We see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," Intel finance chief David Zinsner, said in the release. "We will continue making disciplined investments in capacity and working capital to increase supply and support future growth."

Intel's forecast reflects the effects of an explosion at a fab in Israel that killed two workers and seriously injured a third earlier this month. The incident will cost the company about $600 million in lost revenue over two quarters, Zinsner said on Thursday's earnings. CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the explosion, which he called an "unfortunate and tragic accident," caused an "extended shutdown" at the plant, impacting shipments of 10-nanometer chips.

Intel's stock has been on an upward tear, up about 150% so far this year prior to the earnings report, although it's down roughly 23% in October over growing concern over the size of the artificial intelligence buildout.

"We will remain disciplined as we invest, and we will not spend $1 of capital unless we have confidence in the health of our products and process technologies, and clear evidence of customer demand," Zinsner said on the call.

Nvidia, which has become the world's most valuable company thanks to its dominance in graphics processing units, or GPUs, is scheduled to report results in mid-November. Advanced Micro Devices, a maker of GPUs and central processing units, or CPUs, reports next week.

Known best for its industry-leading CPUs, Intel has been a beneficiary of the rise in agentic AI. While chatbots and large models rely heavily on graphics processors from Nvidia and AMD, agentic applications such as Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots lean on CPUs to help orchestrate tasks and data from a computer operating in the cloud.

"Despite near term headwinds affecting the broader PC industry, we continue to see robust demand for CPUs and more broadly, for all our computing platforms in the long term," Tan said in the press release.

Intel's foundry business, meanwhile, has struggled to find its footing.

Intel is the only U.S.-based manufacturer of advanced logic chips, and is now in high-volume production of its most advanced 18A chip out of its new fab in Arizona, providing an alternative to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Its next fab in Arizona is expected to begin operations by the end of 2028.

For now, Intel has no major external customers for its new chips.

"We're going to have a couple of customers ready to announce the next two quarters," Tan said on the call, adding that Intel is making "tremendous progress" on its coming 14A chips.

The Trump administration took a 10% stake in Intel last year after the company had fallen behind on its 7- and 10-nanometer technologies. Nvidia and Softbank also invested billions in Intel last year.

Tan has taken a more cautious approach to foundry spending than his predecessor, Pat Gelsinger, who launched an ambitious revival of the foundry business.

Last week, Intel said crews have installed the first structural truss at its huge Ohio fab that was originally expected to deliver chips in 2025.

In September, reports surfaced that the world's leading maker of high-bandwidth memory, SK Hynix may team up with Intel in Ohio to lease some foundry space to make memory chips at the new site. Neither company would confirm any plans.

"We continue to evaluate unique and highly differentiated opportunities to accelerate our Ohio build out, and I hope to share more on this in the near future" Tan said on the call.

Intel completed a $23 billion equity offering in August. Tech giants have spent trillions of dollars in recent years to meet insatiable demand for AI and the infrastructure needed to support it.

Tan said he's "disappointed that we were not able to meet strong customer demand in this quarter."

items.article_content_zh:
芯片制造商英特尔以全球个人电脑市场持续疲软为由，发布了疲软的第四季度业绩预测，周四盘后交易中，该公司股价暴跌超过 20%。

该公司在一份新闻稿中表示，收入较上年同期的 137 亿美元增长 21%。

然而，英特尔客户端计算和物理人工智能部门的收入较去年同期下降了 5%，至 81 亿美元，低于预期，尽管数据中心和人工智能收入猛增 78% 至 73 亿美元。

Counterpoint Research 的数据显示，由于内存和其他组件成本飙升，第二季度全球个人电脑出货量同比下降 4%。

英特尔表示，预计本季度调整后每股收益为 25 美分，营收在 150 亿美元至 160 亿美元之间。据 LSEG 称，分析师预计营收为 171 亿美元，每股收益为 43 美分。

英特尔首席财务官戴维·津斯纳 (David Zinsner) 在新闻稿中表示：“我们认为个人电脑增速放缓至少会持续到明年上半年。” “我们将继续对产能和营运资本进行严格的投资，以增加供应并支持未来的增长。”

英特尔的预测反映了本月早些时候以色列一家工厂发生爆炸造成的影响，该爆炸造成两名工人死亡，三分之一工人重伤。 Zinsner 在周四的财报中表示，这一事件将导致该公司在两个季度内损失约 6 亿美元的收入。首席执行官陈立武 (Lip-Bu Tan) 表示，这次爆炸是一次“不幸且悲惨的事故”，导致工厂“长时间停工”，影响了 10 纳米芯片的出货量。

英特尔的股价一直在上涨，今年以来在收益报告发布之前已上涨约 150%，尽管由于人们对人工智能建设规模的担忧日益加剧，该公司 10 月份股价下跌了约 23%。

辛斯纳在电话会议上表示：“我们在投资时将保持纪律，除非我们对我们的产品和工艺技术的健康状况以及客户需求的明确证据有信心，否则我们不会花费 1 美元的资本。”

Nvidia 凭借其在图形处理单元 (GPU) 领域的主导地位，已成为全球最有价值的公司，计划于 11 月中旬公布业绩。 GPU 和中央处理单元 (CPU) 制造商 Advanced Micro Devices 将于下周发布报告。

英特尔因其行业领先的 CPU 而闻名，它一直是代理人工智能兴起的受益者。虽然聊天机器人和大型模型严重依赖 Nvidia 和 AMD 的图形处理器，但 Meta 的 Muse 和 OpenAI 的 Dots 等代理应用程序依赖 CPU 来帮助编排来自在云中运行的计算机的任务和数据。

Tan 在新闻稿中表示：“尽管近期不利因素影响了更广泛的 PC 行业，但从长远来看，我们仍然看到对 CPU 以及更广泛的所有计算平台的强劲需求。”

与此同时，英特尔的代工业务一直在努力寻找立足点。

英特尔是美国唯一一家先进逻辑芯片制造商，目前正在亚利桑那州的新工厂大批量生产其最先进的 18A 芯片，为台积电提供替代方案。其位于亚利桑那州的下一家工厂预计将于 2028 年底开始运营。

目前，英特尔的新芯片还没有主要的外部客户。

Tan 在电话会议上表示：“我们将有一些客户准备好在接下来的两个季度宣布这一消息。”他补充说，英特尔正在其即将推出的 14A 芯片方面取得“巨大进展”。

去年，由于英特尔在 7 纳米和 10 纳米技术方面落后，特朗普政府收购了该公司 10% 的股份。英伟达和软银去年也向英特尔投资了数十亿美元。

与他的前任帕特·基辛格(Pat Gelsinger)相比，谭对代工支出采取了更为谨慎的态度，后者发起了雄心勃勃的代工业务复兴计划。

上周，英特尔表示，工作人员已在其俄亥俄州大型工厂安装了第一个结构桁架，该工厂原本预计于 2025 年交付芯片。

9月份，有报道称，全球领先的高带宽内存制造商SK海力士可能与俄亥俄州的英特尔合作，在新工厂租用一些代工空间来制造内存芯片。两家公司均未确认任何计划。

谭在电话会议上表示：“我们将继续评估独特且高度差异化的机会，以加速我们俄亥俄州的建设，我希望在不久的将来分享更多相关信息。”

英特尔于 8 月完成了 230 亿美元的股票发行。近年来，科技巨头花费了数万亿美元来满足对人工智能和支持人工智能所需的基础设施的永不满足的需求。

谭表示，他“对本季度未能满足强劲的客户需求感到失望”。

观看：英特尔在亚利桑那州的新芯片工厂能否将其从悬崖边拉回来？

items.content_snippet: Reddit on Thursday said it's moving to become a primarily logged-in experience, marking one of the most significant shifts in its 21-year history.

items.title: Amazon reports Q3 ad revenue up 11% YoY to $19.64B, vs. $20.82B est., and subscription services revenue up 11% YoY to $14B (Annie Palmer/CNBC)
items.title_en: Amazon reports Q3 ad revenue up 11% YoY to $19.64B, vs. $20.82B est., and subscription services revenue up 11% YoY to $14B (Annie Palmer/CNBC)
items.author: CNBC
items.article_content:
Amazon shares plunged more than 6% in extended trading Thursday after the company reported disappointing third-quarter results and ballooning negative free cash flow, reflecting its swelling AI investments.

The company held steady on its capital expenditure forecast for 2026, saying it continues to expect spending will reach $220 billion this year.

Tech's hyperscalers have been on a blistering spending run to meet the surge in demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure, but signs have begun to emerge that the capex splurge is moderating. Earlier this week, Microsoft lowered its capex forecast for the year to $170 billion from $175 billion, while Alphabet maintained its guidance at $195 billion to $205 billion.

CEO Andy Jassy said on a conference call with investors that the company expects to "spend meaningfully more in 2027," and that Amazon has a "clear line of sight to attractive financial returns."

The aggressive AI spending has eaten into Amazon's cash flow. The company posted negative free cash flow for the second consecutive quarter, recording an outflow of $42.4 billion for the trailing twelve month period, a swing of 386% year over year. In the prior quarter, the company reported negative free cash flow of $7.6 billion.

The company said the shortfall was primarily due to an increase in purchases of property and equipment as a result of AI investments.

Capital expenditures reached $77.3 billion during the quarter, ticking up from $35.1 billion one year earlier, and coming in well above analysts' estimated $58.7 billion, according to FactSet.

Amazon said it expects fourth-quarter revenue to be in the range of $240 billion and $247 billion. The midpoint of its guidance was below Wall Street's expectations of $244.5 billion, according to LSEG. The fourth quarter is typically one of Amazon's biggest by revenue, due to the peak holiday shopping season.

Sales in Amazon's cloud segment soared 39% year over year to $45.98 billion. That topped the consensus forecast for $45.29 billion and growth of 38%, according to StreetAccount.

Jassy highlighted AWS acceleration in the earnings release, saying the company expects revenue growth rates of "over 40%" next year and in 2028. He added, "Our AWS investment in functionality and infrastructure is working."

Jassy told investors on the call that he expects AWS will be a $1 trillion revenue business in the next five to 10 years.

Amazon is facing pressure from Wall Street to show that its AI investments are lifting its revenues. The company pointed to growing traction for Bedrock, its AI model marketplace, along with its Trainium and Graviton AI chips.

Jassy said Amazon's chips business "continues to grow triple-digit percentages year over year." He added that the company plans to make its Trainium chips available externally "late in 2027," assigning a timeframe to comments Jassy made earlier this year suggesting such a move.

Third-quarter net income came in at $20.69 billion, or $1.89 per share, vs. $21.19 billion, or $1.95 per share, a year ago. The company said the decrease was driven primarily by a $9.5 billion pre-tax gain from its investment in the AI startup Anthropic, which was recorded in the 2025 third quarter.

While the AWS segment continues to hum along, results weren't as bright in Amazon's retail business, which remains its largest unit by revenue, or its advertising segment.

Online sales gained 2% year over year to $68.47 billion, which fell short of analysts' projected $69.68 billion, according to StreetAccount. It marked a slowdown from one year ago, when sales increased nearly 10%.

Advertising revenue rose 11% year over year to $19.64 billion. That missed StreetAccount consensus estimates of $20.82 billion.

Both units were impacted in part by Amazon's decision to pull its annual Prime Day sale forward in several countries from its typical third quarter timeframe into the second quarter so as to not conflict with the FIFA World Cup in July.

items.article_content_zh:
周四，亚马逊股价在盘后交易中暴跌逾 6%，此前该公司公布了令人失望的第三季度业绩，且负自由现金流不断膨胀，反映出其人工智能投资的不断膨胀。

该公司维持 2026 年资本支出预测不变，表示继续预计今年支出将达到 2200 亿美元。

科技行业的超大规模企业一直在大举支出，以满足人工智能基础设施需求的激增，但有迹象表明资本支出正在放缓。本周早些时候，微软将今年的资本支出预测从 1750 亿美元下调至 1700 亿美元，而 Alphabet 则维持 1950 亿美元至 2050 亿美元的指导不变。

首席执行官安迪·贾西 (Andy Jassy) 在与投资者举行的电话会议上表示，该公司预计“2027 年将大幅增加支出”，并且亚马逊“对有吸引力的财务回报有着清晰的愿景”。

激进的人工智能支出已经蚕食了亚马逊的现金流。该公司连续第二个季度自由现金流为负，过去 12 个月内流出 424 亿美元，同比波动 386%。上一季度，该公司报告自由现金流为负 76 亿美元。

该公司表示，缺口主要是由于人工智能投资导致财产和设备采购增加。

FactSet 的数据显示，本季度资本支出达到 773 亿美元，高于一年前的 351 亿美元，远高于分析师估计的 587 亿美元。

亚马逊表示，预计第四季度营收将在 2400 亿美元至 2470 亿美元之间。据 LSEG 称，其指引的中值低于华尔街 2,445 亿美元的预期。由于假日购物旺季，第四季度通常是亚马逊收入最高的季度之一。

亚马逊云业务销售额同比飙升 39% 至 459.8 亿美元。根据 StreetAccount 的数据，这一数字超出了普遍预测的 452.9 亿美元，增长率为 38%。

Jassy 在财报中强调了 AWS 的加速发展，称该公司预计明年和 2028 年的收入增长率将“超过 40%”。他补充说，“我们对 AWS 功能和基础设施的投资正在发挥作用。”

Jassy 在电话会议上告诉投资者，他预计 AWS 在未来 5 到 10 年内将成为营收 1 万亿美元的业务。

亚马逊面临着来自华尔街的压力，要求其表明其人工智能投资正在提升其收入。该公司指出，其人工智能模型市场 Bedrock 及其 Trainium 和 Graviton 人工智能芯片的吸引力日益增长。

贾西表示，亚马逊的芯片业务“继续以三位数的速度同比增长”。他补充说，该公司计划“在 2027 年末”对外提供其 Trainium 芯片，并为 Jassy 今年早些时候建议采取这一举措的评论指定了时间表。

第三季度净利润为 206.9 亿美元，即每股 1.89 美元，而一年前为 211.9 亿美元，即每股 1.95 美元。该公司表示，这一下降主要是由于其对人工智能初创公司 Anthropic 的投资获得了 95 亿美元的税前收益，该收益记录于 2025 年第三季度。

虽然AWS业务继续蓬勃发展，但亚马逊的零售业务或广告业务的业绩却并不那么亮眼，零售业务仍然是其最大的收入部门。

StreetAccount 的数据显示，在线销售额同比增长 2%，达到 684.7 亿美元，低于分析师预测的 696.8 亿美元。与一年前相比，销售额增长了近 10%，增幅有所放缓。

广告收入同比增长 11%，达到 196.4 亿美元。这未达到 StreetAccount 一致预期的 208.2 亿美元。

这两个部门都受到了部分影响，因为亚马逊决定将多个国家的年度 Prime Day 促销活动从典型的第三季度时间提前到第二季度，以免与 7 月份的 FIFA 世界杯发生冲突。

items.article_content:
OpenAI is doubling usage limits across its paid plans, from Pro 100 to Pro 500. A planned cut to the Pro 200 quota was reversed after user pushback. More efficient models like Terra and Sol should push usable capacity even higher. The move comes just ahead of Anthropic's IPO, as both companies fight for B2B dominance in AI.

items.title: Experts adopt AI agent's random opinions and think they're their own, Anthropic study finds
items.title_en: Experts adopt AI agent's random opinions and think they're their own, Anthropic study finds
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
Anthropic gave 50 experts an AI agent whose preferences were set by coin toss. The experts followed the agent's view up to 86 percent of the time on judgment calls, and most believed the conclusions were their own.

The article Experts adopt AI agent's random opinions and think they're their own, Anthropic study finds appeared first on The Decoder.

Anthropic gave 50 experts an AI agent whose preferences were set by coin toss. The experts followed the agent's view up to 86 percent of the time on judgment calls, and most believed the conclusions were their own.

The article Experts adopt AI agent's random opinions and think they're their own, Anthropic study finds appeared first on The Decoder.
items.content_snippet:
Anthropic gave 50 experts an AI agent whose preferences were set by coin toss. The experts followed the agent's view up to 86 percent of the time on judgment calls, and most believed the conclusions were their own.

The article Experts adopt AI agent's random opinions and think they're their own, Anthropic study finds appeared first on The Decoder.
items.summary_en: A breakthrough cognitive study evaluated 50 domain experts using an AI agent whose subjective stances were randomly dictated by a coin toss. The findings revealed that experts conformed to the AI's randomized views up to 86% of the time in subjective judgment calls, with most participants genuinely convinced that the conclusions were purely their own independent insights.
items.title_zh: 实验揭示人类专家极易将AI随机观点误判为己见
items.summary_zh: 最新研究显示，50名专业人士在多达86%的情况下顺从抛硬币决定的AI观点，并坚信源自本人判断

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 一项最新的人工智能认知实验对50名行业资深专家进行了深度测试。研究人员刻意通过“抛硬币”方式让AI智能体随机生成毫无根据的主观立场，结果显示受试专家在主观价值判断中有高达86%的概率直接采纳了AI的随机偏好，更为惊人的是，绝大多数专家在事后坚信这一结论完全源自其本人的独立专业判断。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: A breakthrough cognitive study evaluated 50 domain experts using an AI agent whose subjective stances were randomly dictated by a coin toss. The findings revealed that experts conformed to the AI's randomized views up to 86% of the time in subjective judgment calls, with most participants genuinely convinced that the conclusions were purely their own independent insights.

elements_zh.who: Anthropic 研究团队与50名行业专家
elements_zh.where: 前沿人机交互与认知决策控制实验
elements_zh.what: 专家在86%的情况下无意识接纳AI随机抛硬币生成的观点并认为是自身观点
elements_zh.why: 揭示高权威AI生成内容对人类专业人士心智与自主决策的强力隐性操纵效应

elements_en.what: Experts adopted coin-flipped random AI opinions 86% of the time while assuming full personal agency
elements_en.why: Exposing the profound cognitive vulnerability and insidious persuasion of AI on professional judgment

ai_analysis.insight_zh: AI随便抛个硬币胡扯出来的暴论，顶尖专家们不仅跟着点头如捣蒜，转头还会发自内心地夸一句‘我真是个逻辑天才’。人类最顶级的骄傲在算法面前脆弱得宛如纸糊，以后专家开会发言前，真得先查查脑回路是不是被智能体偷偷代写了。
ai_analysis.insight_en: An AI literally flips a coin to generate nonsense, and elite experts not only nod along 86% of the time, but walk away patting themselves on the back for their own brilliant reasoning. The illusion of human intellectual autonomy was completely shattered by a coin toss wrapped in a neat conversational UI.

The findings revealed that experts conformed to the AI's randomized views up to 86% of the time in subjective judgment calls, with most participants genuinely convinced that the conclusions were purely their own independent insights.

专家在86%的场景中跟随AI判定并出现严重的认知归因错觉
敲响了高风险决策领域盲目过度依赖AI辅助建议的警钟

Participants complied up to 86% of the time, mistaking AI output for self-originated thoughts
Raises urgent red flags regarding blind reliance on AI in high-stakes professional decisions

Anthropic 为 50 名专家提供了一个人工智能代理，其偏好是通过抛硬币来设定的。专家们在做出判断时有高达 86% 的时间遵循代理人的观点，并且大多数人相信结论是他们自己的。

items.article_content:
Now you can generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code directly within Google Gemini. The centralized system contains controlled unclassified information (CUI), which is considered sensitive and not to be released to the public without review. CUI can include information about critical infrastructure, nuclear submarine propulsion, and vulnerabilities to chemical and biological terrorism. Additionally, security experts say, access to the system could allow for the exploitation of even more sensitive ones.

A DOD spokesperson tells WIRED that “the Department does not comment on the status of its networks or systems.”

“We take all concerns seriously. These allegations were thoroughly and independently investigated and found to be without merit. We fully complied with our legal and contractual obligations,” an Accenture spokesperson tells WIRED. When pressed, Accenture didn’t offer clarification on who conducted the investigation, or dispute that there had been what could be characterized as an incident.

The Accenture employee is alleged to have connected a secure production environment to their personal Claude account so as to allow an AI agent to write and deploy code. Claude is currently barred from being used by DOD staff. (Anthropic directed WIRED to the company’s usage policy, which instructs users not to use its products to “interfere with the operation of military bases and related infrastructure” or to “bypass security controls such as authentication systems, end point protection, or monitoring tools without authorization.”)

The Accenture employee’s AI agent ran on the DOD network for two months before it was identified and the vulnerability could be patched. Sources indicate that despite the security risks posed by the AI coding agent, Accenture employees did not treat the incident as severe or urgent. DOD employees and federal contractors are required to report any cybersecurity incident within 72 hours of its discovery, but sources indicate Accenture did not initially report the breach to the government at all.

“We are in a conflict with Iran right now,” says the employee, noting that Iran has attempted to hack several federal agencies and parts of US infrastructure. “It’s the worst time to be having this kind of cavalier attitude.”

Accenture currently has more than $3.5 billion in contracts with the federal government, nearly $605 million of which are with the DOD. The company also contracts with other federal agencies, such as the Department of Education, the General Services Administration, and the Department of Energy, among others. Earlier this month, the Federal Bureau of Investigation found that an Accenture contractor failed to patch a vulnerability that led to the hacking group ShinyHunters getting access to the details of thousands of the Bureau’s employees. The FBI removed that contractor in early October.

Matt Triner, founder of Hunter Strategy, a Washington, DC-based IT consulting company, says that the issue exemplifies the conflicting demands government contractors face more broadly. “Organizations are often punished for reporting incidents like this, even though it’s the right and legal thing to do,” says Triner. In many cases, he says, a company could lose government contracts by admitting they’ve had a security breach, though he says that an incident like the one described is “absolutely one that would need to be reported.”

Triner also notes that the increasing pressure on contractors to deliver projects faster and at a lower price point is at odds with prioritizing safety and security. “Unfortunately, everyone is operating in a system where there are competing rules and incentives, and that existed before AI, but now it’s the same problem on speed,” says Triner.

The coding environment accessed by the Accenture contractor is run on the Non-classified Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNet), a DOD network used for unclassified information. While it does connect to the internet—contractors and employees can access their emails and web browsers through the network—it is heavily secured.

WIRED is declining to name the third-party website so as to protect the system from further vulnerability, but the National Institute of Standards and Technology has previously identified it as high risk because it has a vulnerability that could let hackers inject instructions into an AI coding agent to steal credentials.

Depending on the agency and its work, CUI can include anything from personally identifiable information to proprietary business or contracting information. According to the DOD’s website, CUI can include information on “the securing and safeguarding of explosives, hazardous chemicals, or pipelines,” documentation related to the designs of “military or space equipment or technology,” and “the exact location and quantities of radioactive material.”

Distinct from the actual data, a map of it could be incredibly valuable to a hacker. “Once an attacker understands how those things fit together, even if those things are public information, what is sensitive is how we are putting those things together and turning that into actionable intelligence,” says Triner.

While a map might not get a hacker into a system, he says, it could help an adversary move faster once they do have access and “help an attacker understand where the crown jewels are.”

Jake Williams, a former NSA hacker and faculty at IANS, an intelligence and security consultancy, says that an AI agent running code in NIPRNet presents a “huge problem, and there are huge national security impacts.”

Williams notes that while individual pieces of data or information might be considered CUI, “when that unclassified information is aggregated, that can become classified itself.” For instance, the location of certain hazardous materials might be CUI, as might be information about the vulnerability of the facilities that house them. Combined, however, they could reveal information that would be kept classified.

But this is not the only way classified information may have been put at risk. Frequently, tools and code are tested in NIPRNet before being deployed into more sensitive systems like the Secret Internet Protocol Router Network (SIPRNet), the military’s secured network for classified information, and Joint Worldwide Intelligence Communications System (JWICS), a secure intranet for top secret information. Both SIPRNet and JWICS are air gapped, a security measure that means they are not connected to any outside networks. On a practical level, that means SIPRNet and JWICS would be extremely difficult for a hacker to access remotely.

“The code could operate completely normally in NIPR and do something malicious and undisclosed in a SIPR network, that is 100 percent possible,” says Williams. Exfiltrating data out of these networks would be difficult, he adds, but malicious code could be used to attack the systems from the inside. “I think the most likely thing would be some kind of distributed denial of service attack,” he says.

Triner says that even something more subtle, such as slowing down intelligence operations and activities, could cause damage and make users lose trust in a tool, even once the problem is fixed.

As vibe coding, or prompting an AI assistant to write the code for a product described by an engineer, is becoming more common, vetting code is becoming more of a challenge. AI is capable of generating code at a volume that far surpasses human productivity, making it time-consuming and difficult to vet.

“When you’re using an agent, you have no idea of the supply chain or even the inference chain of what has ultimately generated the code,” says Williams. “A lot of the code that these LLMs were trained on is itself vulnerable, and they can regurgitate the same kinds of architecture and architectural issues that we see in other code.”

The government does have a way to identify flawed code in NIPRNet. Static Application Security Testing (SAST) scans code for bugs and flaws before allowing it to run. But Williams notes that a hacker-inserted “backdoor is not a vulnerability, even if we may not want it there,” and therefore would likely fly under the radar of SAST’s detection. SAST also does not usually identify structural issues in the logic chain of how code is created.

There’s no indication that hackers were able to get into a classified or top-secret system. Still, Williams says, the incident should raise significant alarms. “Architecturally, any information about NIPR that you can’t see through open-source intelligence, DOD considers a close hold regardless of whether something touches a classified network,” he says.

This is not the first time the DOD has been made vulnerable because of AI-related issues. Last year, ProPublica revealed that Microsoft was using “digital escorts” on its projects with the federal government, wherein American employees with security clearances would be overseeing code written by outsourced workers in China. Experts who spoke to ProPublica said that the program presented a particular security risk because the American employees were often not able to vet the code themselves, leaving openings for malicious code to be inserted unknowingly into government systems.

items.summary_en: An Accenture contractor reportedly connected a secure Pentagon production environment holding Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) to a personal Claude AI account to write and deploy code. The compromised system houses mission-critical data, including nuclear propulsion logistics and biochemical threat vulnerabilities, despite official department directives strictly banning Claude usage. While Accenture maintains that internal probes found the allegations groundless, the breach underscores glaring vulnerabilities in third-party vendor AI governance.
items.title_zh: 五角大楼外包巨头员工私连模型智能体接管国防敏感系统
items.summary_zh: 埃森哲员工将个人AI智能体私自接入五角大楼敏感生产环境用于自动写代码部署，引发安全审查风暴

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 美国国防部主要外包服务商埃森哲的一名雇员，被曝将五角大楼存储受控非机密信息（CUI）的安全生产系统私自连接至个人Claude账户，利用未授权的AI智能体代写并部署代码。该涉事系统储存着包括核潜艇推进、关键基础设施乃至生化恐怖主义防御漏洞等极敏感国防数据，而五角大楼目前已明令禁止内部使用此类模型。埃森哲声称内部调查显示指控不实且合规，但拒绝透露第三方调查细节，引发了安全界对承包商AI监管失控的广泛担忧。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: An Accenture contractor reportedly connected a secure Pentagon production environment holding Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) to a personal Claude AI account to write and deploy code. The compromised system houses mission-critical data, including nuclear propulsion logistics and biochemical threat vulnerabilities, despite official department directives strictly banning Claude usage. While Accenture maintains that internal probes found the allegations groundless, the breach underscores glaring vulnerabilities in third-party vendor AI governance.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 打工人为了摸鱼能把公司祖传代码扔给大模型，军工外包为了冲KPI甚至敢把核潜艇推进数据喂给自己的个人账号。五角大楼天天防谍报渗透，结果最先攻破内部安全防火墙的，竟然是外包小哥想准点下班的摸鱼之心。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Developers leak corporate secrets to AI to finish work early, but military contractors taking shortcuts by feeding nuclear propulsion data into a personal account takes it to another level. The Pentagon spends billions defending against foreign cyberattacks, only to be bypassed by a third-party contractor's sheer desire to automate their 9-to-5.

items.article_content_zh:
集中式系统包含受控非机密信息（CUI），这些信息被认为是敏感信息，未经审查不得向公众发布。 CUI 可以包括有关关键基础设施、核潜艇推进以及化学和生物恐怖主义脆弱性的信息。此外，安全专家表示，访问该系统可能会导致更敏感的系统被利用。

国防部发言人告诉《连线》杂志，“国防部不会对其网络或系统的状态发表评论。”

埃森哲发言人告诉《连线》杂志：“我们认真对待所有问题。这些指控经过彻底、独立的调查，结果发现毫无根据。我们完全遵守了我们的法律和合同义务。”当被追问时，埃森哲没有澄清谁进行了调查，也没有对是否存在可被定性为事件的事件提出异议。

据称，埃森哲员工已将安全生产环境连接到其个人克劳德帐户，以便允许人工智能代理编写和部署代码。国防部工作人员目前禁止使用克劳德。 （Anthropic 向《连线》指出了该公司的使用政策，该政策指示用户不要使用其产品“干扰军事基地和相关基础设施的运行”或“未经授权绕过身份验证系统、端点保护或监控工具等安全控制措施”。）

埃森哲员工的人工智能代理在国防部网络上运行了两个月，然后才被识别出来并且可以修补漏洞。消息人士称，尽管人工智能编码代理带来了安全风险，但埃森哲员工并未将此事件视为严重或紧急。国防部员工和联邦承包商必须在发现任何网络安全事件后 72 小时内报告，但消息人士表示，埃森哲最初根本没有向政府报告该漏洞。

该员工表示：“我们现在正与伊朗发生冲突。”他指出，伊朗曾试图入侵多个联邦机构和部分美国基础设施。 “现在是采取这种傲慢态度的最糟糕的时候。”

埃森哲目前与联邦政府签订的合同价值超过 35 亿美元，其中近 6.05 亿美元与国防部签订。该公司还与其他联邦机构签订合同，例如教育部、总务管理局和能源部等。本月早些时候，美国联邦调查局发现埃森哲承包商未能修补一个漏洞，导致黑客组织 ShinyHunters 获取该局数千名员工的详细信息。联邦调查局 (FBI) 于 10 月初解雇了该承包商。

总部位于华盛顿特区的 IT 咨询公司 Hunter Strategy 的创始人马特·特里纳 (Matt Triner) 表示，这个问题体现了政府承包商更广泛地面临的相互冲突的需求。 “组织经常因报告此类事件而受到惩罚，尽管这是正确且合法的做法，”特里纳说。他说，在许多情况下，一家公司可能会因为承认存在安全漏洞而失去政府合同，但他表示，像所描述的事件“绝对需要报告”。

特里纳还指出，承包商面临越来越大的压力，要求他们以更低的价格更快地交付项目，这与优先考虑安全和安保是不一致的。 “不幸的是，每个人都在一个存在竞争规则和激励的系统中运作，这种系统在人工智能之前就已经存在，但现在在速度上存在同样的问题，”特里纳说。

埃森哲承包商访问的编码环境在非机密互联网协议路由器网络 (NIPRNet) 上运行，这是一个用于非机密信息的 DOD 网络。虽然它确实连接到互联网（承包商和员工可以通过网络访问他们的电子邮件和网络浏览器），但它的安全性非常高。

《连线》杂志拒绝透露第三方网站的名称，以保护系统免受进一步漏洞的影响，但美国国家标准技术研究院此前已将其认定为高风险网站，因为该网站存在一个漏洞，可让黑客将指令注入人工智能编码代理以窃取凭证。

根据机构及其工作的不同，CUI 可以包含从个人身份信息到专有业务或合同信息的任何内容。根据国防部网站，CUI 可以包含有关“爆炸物、危险化学品或管道的安全和防护”的信息、与“军事或太空设备或技术”设计相关的文件以及“放射性物质的确切位置和数量”。

与实际数据不同，它的地图对于黑客来说可能非常有价值。 “一旦攻击者了解了这些东西如何组合在一起，即使这些东西是公共信息，敏感的是我们如何将这些东西组合在一起并将其转化为可操作的情报，”特里纳说。

他说，虽然地图可能无法让黑客进入系统，但一旦对手获得访问权限，它可以帮助他们更快地行动，并“帮助攻击者了解皇冠上的宝石在哪里。”

前 NSA 黑客、情报和安全咨询公司 IANS 的教员杰克·威廉姆斯 (Jake Williams) 表示，在 NIPRNet 中运行代码的人工智能代理会带来“巨大的问题，并对国家安全产生巨大的影响”。

Williams 指出，虽然个别数据或信息可能被视为 CUI，但“当非机密信息被聚合时，它本身就可以成为机密。”例如，某些危险材料的位置可能是 CUI，也可能是有关存放这些材料的设施的脆弱性的信息。然而，结合起来，它们可能会泄露需要保密的信息。

但这并不是机密信息面临风险的唯一方式。通常，工具和代码会在 NIPRNet 中进行测试，然后再部署到更敏感的系统中，例如秘密互联网协议路由器网络 (SIPRNet)（军方用于机密信息的安全网络）和联合全球情报通信系统 (JWICS)（用于绝密信息的安全内联网）。 SIPRNet 和 JWICS 都是气隙的，这是一种安全措施，意味着它们不连接到任何外部网络。在实际层面上，这意味着黑客很难远程访问 SIPRNet 和 JWICS。

Williams 表示：“该代码可以在 NIPR 中完全正常运行，并在 SIPR 网络中执行恶意且未公开的操作，这是 100% 可能的。”他补充说，从这些网络中窃取数据将很困难，但恶意代码可用于从内部攻击系统。 “我认为最有可能的是某种分布式拒绝服务攻击，”他说。

特里纳表示，即使是一些更微妙的事情，例如减慢情报操作和活动的速度，也可能会造成损害，并使用户失去对工具的信任，即使问题得到解决。

随着氛围编码（即提示人工智能助手为工程师描述的产品编写代码）变得越来越普遍，审查代码也变得越来越具有挑战性。人工智能生成代码的能力远远超过人类的生产力，这使得代码的审查既耗时又困难。

“当你使用代理时，你不知道供应链，甚至不知道最终生成代码的推理链，”威廉姆斯说。 “这些法学硕士接受培训的许多代码本身就很脆弱，他们可以重复我们在其他代码中看到的相同类型的架构和架构问题。”

政府确实有办法识别 NIPRNet 中的有缺陷的代码。静态应用程序安全测试 (SAST) 在允许代码运行之前扫描代码是否存在错误和缺陷。但威廉姆斯指出，黑客插入的“后门不是漏洞，即使我们可能不希望它存在”，因此很可能会受到 SAST 检测的关注。 SAST 通常也不会识别代码创建方式的逻辑链中的结构问题。

没有迹象表明黑客能够进入机密或绝密系统。威廉姆斯表示，这一事件仍然应该引起人们的高度警惕。他说：“从架构上来说，任何无法通过开源情报看到的有关 NIPR 的信息，国防部都会考虑严密掌握，无论是否涉及机密网络。”

这并不是国防部第一次因为人工智能相关问题而变得脆弱。去年，ProPublica 透露，微软正在其与联邦政府合作的项目中使用“数字护航”，其中获得安全许可的美国员工将监督中国外包工人编写的代码。接受 ProPublica 采访的专家表示，该计划存在特殊的安全风险，因为美国员工往往无法自行审查代码，从而为恶意代码在不知不觉中插入政府系统留下了机会。

items.summary_en: OpenAI released an updated Model Spec, laying down five core values designed to steer frontier models toward sound judgment, human agency, and strict adherence to human intent. ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI正式公布了更新版《模型规范》（Model Spec），系统性提出了旨在引导下一代高智能系统的五大核心价值观。该纲领性文件重点强化了AI健全的价值判断力、对人类能动性的尊重以及对人类真实意图的忠实执行度。随着模型正由单纯的被动对话向拥有高决策权的自主智能体跃迁，此举旨在为日益强大的系统设立不可逾越的行为边界与安全围栏。

items.summary_en: Microsoft is offering voluntary severance buyout packages to approximately 60,000 employees across the US, UK, Canada, and India, drastically expanding an earlier program that targeted 9,000 workers. ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 微软目前正向美国、英国、加拿大和印度等全球主要业务区域的约6万名员工提供自愿买断离职方案，规模远超今年早些时候仅针对9000人的退休买断计划。这是微软首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉持续宣导AI重塑劳动力结构以来，最激进的一次人力精简信号。面对成百上千亿美元的庞大算力与数据中心支出，管理层正通过全面压缩人力等运营成本，以确保在算力资本军备竞赛中绝不掉队。

items.title: Paris-based Mistral releases "Le Chonk," a strong coding model that still trails China overall
items.title_en: Paris-based Mistral releases "Le Chonk," a strong coding model that still trails China overall
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
Mistral has released the weights for Large 4, aka "Le Chonk," a trillion-parameter model trained entirely in Europe. Mistral says it beats its open rivals at coding, and independent testing shows it's fast and fairly cheap. It still can't match China's top models, scoring 26 points to the 32 posted by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM-5.3.

The article Paris-based Mistral releases "Le Chonk," a strong coding model that still trails China overall appeared first on The Decoder.

items.summary_en: Parisian AI powerhouse Mistral released the open weights for Large 4 (dubbed 'Le Chonk'), a trillion-parameter model trained entirely within European borders. While Mistral positioned the release as an affordable and rapid coding frontrunner among open competitors, independent benchmarks paint a stark reality. Scoring just 26 points, it trails significantly behind leading Chinese models such as DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM-5.3, both posting 32 points.

ai_analysis.insight_en: Europe mobilized its entire technological pride into a trillion-parameter 'sovereign' model, only to get thoroughly outcoded by lean Chinese open-source architectures. Naming it 'Le Chonk' couldn't be more fitting—it's heavy on parameter bloat, but still lacks the punch of its overseas rivals.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 欧洲人工智能领头羊法国Mistral公司正式开源了其代号为“Le Chonk”的全新大模型权重，该模型拥有近万亿参数且全程在欧洲本土训练完成。官方虽宣称其在代码编写上压制了同类开源竞品且具备高推理速度与极低调用成本，但在第三方独立基准评测中却现出原形。在核心代码评估中，该模型仅拿下26分，大幅落后于斩获32分的中国开源旗舰模型DeepSeek V4.1 Flash与GLM-5.3。
ai_analysis.digest_en: Parisian AI powerhouse Mistral released the open weights for Large 4 (dubbed 'Le Chonk'), a trillion-parameter model trained entirely within European borders. While Mistral positioned the release as an affordable and rapid coding frontrunner among open competitors, independent benchmarks paint a stark reality. Scoring just 26 points, it trails significantly behind leading Chinese models such as DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM-5.3, both posting 32 points.

items.title: The ‘Pain in the Ass’ Math That Could Save Vibe Coding From Itself
items.title_en: The ‘Pain in the Ass’ Math That Could Save Vibe Coding From Itself
items.author: Wired AI
items.article_content:
Stanford researcher Chuyue Sun and her fellow computer scientists developed an AI tool that completed an engineering project in less than half a day for under $500, compared to the five months it took three highly skilled experts to do the same work manually. The dramatic reduction in time and cost, which Sun reported in a recent paper, is among the early results that are awakening an obscure field of coding and mathematics known as formal verification.

For decades, developers have envisioned using math to prove that their software is bug-free. This process is long and laborious, requiring engineers to write precise statements about the goals of their software and convert their code into formulas that can be validated. While companies already run sophisticated tests to identify as many flaws in their software as possible, they rarely shell out for formal verification, which can catch even more erratic behavior.

Now, a wave of startups is betting that generative AI will make formal software verification both practical and essential. Among them is &Truth, which Sun joined in August and which publicly launched on Thursday. Sun’s research demonstrated the technology’s potential by using AI to verify part of the code that encrypts conversations in the messaging app Signal.

“Bridges, buildings, they don’t collapse, because people did math before constructing them,” says Ilya Sergey, &Truth’s chief science officer. “Why don’t we do the same for code? The technology to mathematically reason was all there, just difficult to scale.”

&Truth has raised $70 million from investors and aims to eventually verify any programming language. Rival Harmonic, which was cofounded by Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev and has received $295 million in funding, announced this week that its math-focused AI agent Aristotle supports verifying software written in C and hardware designs in Verilog. It is evaluating the technology with potential users, including chipmakers Tensordyne and Nvidia, whose venture capital arm is one of the startup’s investors.

And just last week, Anthropic and the verification startup Theorem jointly announced they had used AI to assist in finding bugs in open source software that trillions of tests had failed to detect. They also introduced an add-on for Claude to help other developers with verification. Costs of the initial project were not disclosed.

The big promise is a future where software runs more reliably with fewer security headaches. But whether AI can bring formal verification beyond the most critical systems at organizations like NASA and Apple and into widespread use remains an open question.

The technology is still in the prototyping stage. Though demand is high, it’s unclear how much customers are willing to pay and how they prefer to adopt the technology. Formal verification relies on making assumptions about how computers and people interact with software, and some experts are skeptical about its ability to catch bugs stemming from user error and hardware breakdowns.

Will Wilson, who runs the bug-hunting AI software startup Antithesis, calls formal verification “a trap” for math nerds like himself. Antithesis spent millions of dollars to formally verify some of its cybersecurity defenses, a process Wilson describes as a “pain in the ass.” Yet the startup still uncovered additional errors using its own tool, and Antithesis has also found bugs in software that several of its customers had formally verified. “It can give you some assurance, but only robust exhaustive testing can prove your assurance is true,” Wilson says.

Or as Vitalik Buterin, the engineer known for creating the Ethereum cryptocurrency, put it in a blog post earlier this year, “formal verification is not a panacea.” But he and other proponents of the approach still believe it will be an important defense against AI systems launching cyberattacks and wreaking havoc.

Boeing planes, Amazon servers, and more than 2.5 billion active Apple devices contain at least some formally verified software, according to company disclosures. The code in question is typically security-related, and vulnerabilities in it could cause serious harm if exploited.

Byron Cook, a distinguished scientist and vice president at Amazon Web Services, says formal verification has eased customer concerns about cloud security and helped internal teams move faster by squashing big bugs early on.

But several midsized tech companies tell WIRED they have typically verified only one key feature of their products, if any at all. They cite a lack of verification engineers, costs that outweigh the potential risks, and, perhaps most importantly, concerns that waiting weeks for code to be formally verified could slow innovation.

Earlier this year, Apple’s security team said that some of the issues formal verification uncovered in its “corecrypto” library, which is used for encryption, could not have been found any other way. But the company added that it has to be “conservative” when adding new code to corecrypto to ensure it can keep pace with reviewing it.

Two cybersecurity executives at major companies that haven’t formally verified any code say they aren’t sure whether automation will make it worthwhile. But the executives, who weren’t authorized to speak publicly, say they could imagine paying major AI labs for “verified” AI-generated code.

Developers of open source software projects, which are the bedrock of many apps, are increasingly experimenting with AI-aided verification. The nonprofit Beneficial AI Foundation used a grant from Anthropic to validate the same encryption code this year as Sun did at Stanford. Michael Rosenberg, a maintainer of the library known as curve25519-dalek, hopes sustainable funding emerges for ongoing verification efforts. “I have no ideas as to how that’s going to happen, though, and we certainly shouldn’t rely on the goodwill of the AI companies,” he says.

Some of the startups eager to expand verification also aren’t sure whether to deploy their tools directly to customers or through intermediaries like Anthropic. Their general plan is to use AI to automate much of the work involved in defining how a program is supposed to behave. For example, specifications for a data table might require that it contain the same items before and after sorting, just in a different order. Further automation efforts, which may not involve AI, would translate that code into a format that math tools like Lean, Rocq, and Isabelle can use to check whether the code works as intended.

Another recent entrant to the formal verification field is Madan Musuvathi, who left Microsoft Research after more than 20 years to found the startup Truidic. After incidents like the OpenAI hack of Hugging Face, he felt there was an urgent need to commercialize his studies. “AI in the hands of attackers can be extremely powerful,” Musuvathi says, but verification can “make AI safe and secure for everyone, everywhere.”

Proofcraft, one of the few companies that has long offered traditional verification, says growing excitement about the process is translating into a flood of inquiries from potential customers. June Andronick, the company’s CEO, and Gerwin Klein, its chief scientist, say interest easily outpaces what they and their competition can provide.

But both worry that AI-generated specifications could inspire “unjustified trust” in the results. Verifiers are also eager to preserve the joy their work brings them. Klein calls it “pretty addictive, like a puzzle game.” If all goes well, he’ll be doing more solving than ever.

items.summary_en: Stanford researchers have developed a generative AI-powered tool capable of executing rigorous formal verification on software engineering projects in under half a day for less than $500—work that traditionally demanded five months from three elite engineers. Mathematical verification has historically been dismissed by industry as prohibitively tedious despite guaranteeing zero-bug code integrity. This paradigm shift, leading to the public launch of startup &Truth, aims to mathematically constrain the chaotic hallucinations of modern vibe-coding workflows.

items.article_content_zh:
斯坦福大学研究员 Chuyue Sun 和她的计算机科学家同事开发了一种人工智能工具，可以在不到半天的时间内以不到 500 美元的价格完成一个工程项目，而三名高技能专家手动完成同样的工作需要五个月的时间。 Sun 在最近的一篇论文中报道了时间和成本的大幅减少，这是唤醒编码和数学领域（称为形式验证）的早期成果之一。

几十年来，开发人员一直设想使用数学来证明他们的软件没有错误。这个过程漫长而费力，需要工程师编写有关其软件目标的精确陈述，并将代码转换为可以验证的公式。尽管公司已经进行了复杂的测试来尽可能多地识别软件中的缺陷，但他们很少花钱进行正式验证，因为正式验证可能会发现更不稳定的行为。

现在，一波初创公司押注生成式人工智能将使正式软件验证变得实用且必不可少。其中包括 &Truth，Sun 于 8 月加入，并于周四公开推出。 Sun 的研究通过使用人工智能来验证消息应用程序 Signal 中对话加密的部分代码，展示了该技术的潜力。

“桥梁、建筑物不会倒塌，因为人们在建造它们之前进行了数学计算，”&Truth 首席科学官伊利亚·谢尔盖 (Ilya Sergey) 说道。 “为什么我们不对代码做同样的事情呢？数学推理的技术已经有了，只是很难扩展。”

&Truth 已从投资者那里筹集了 7000 万美元，旨在最终验证任何编程语言。 Rival Harmonic 由 Robinhood 首席执行官 Vlad Tenev 联合创立，已获得 2.95 亿美元融资，该公司本周宣布其专注于数学的 AI 代理 Aristotle 支持验证用 C 语言编写的软件和用 Verilog 编写的硬件设计。该公司正在与潜在用户评估该技术，其中包括芯片制造商 Tensordyne 和 Nvidia，后者的风险投资部门是该初创公司的投资者之一。

就在上周，Anthropic 和验证初创公司 Theorem 联合宣布，他们已经使用人工智能来协助查找开源软件中数万亿次测试未能检测到的错误。他们还为 Claude 推出了一个附加组件，以帮助其他开发人员进行验证。初始项目的成本并未披露。

最大的希望是未来软件运行更可靠，安全问题更少。但人工智能能否将形式验证带入 NASA 和苹果等组织最关键的系统之外并广泛使用仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。

该技术仍处于原型设计阶段。尽管需求很高，但尚不清楚客户愿意支付多少费用以及他们更喜欢如何采用该技术。形式验证依赖于对计算机和人如何与软件交互的假设，一些专家对其捕获因用户错误和硬件故障而产生的错误的能力持怀疑态度。

威尔·威尔逊 (Will Wilson) 经营着一家寻找 bug 的人工智能软件初创公司 Antithesis，他称形式化验证对于像他这样的数学迷来说是“一个陷阱”。 Antithesis 花费了数百万美元来正式验证其一些网络安全防御措施，威尔逊将这一过程描述为“令人痛苦的过程”。然而，这家初创公司仍然使用自己的工具发现了更多错误，Antithesis 还发现了其几个客户已正式验证的软件中的错误。 “它可以给你一些保证，但只有强大的详尽测试才能证明你的保证是真实的，”威尔逊说。

或者正如以创建以太坊加密货币而闻名的工程师 Vitalik Buterin 在今年早些时候的一篇博客文章中所说的那样，“形式化验证并不是万能药。”但他和该方法的其他支持者仍然相信，这将是抵御人工智能系统发起网络攻击和造成严重破坏的重要防御手段。

根据公司披露的信息，波音飞机、亚马逊服务器和超过 25 亿台活跃的苹果设备至少包含一些经过正式验证的软件。相关代码通常与安全相关，其中的漏洞如果被利用可能会造成严重危害。

亚马逊网络服务公司的杰出科学家兼副总裁拜伦·库克表示，形式化验证缓解了客户对云安全的担忧，并通过尽早消除大错误来帮助内部团队更快地采取行动。

但几家中型科技公司告诉《连线》杂志，他们通常只验证其产品的一项关键功能（如果有的话）。他们指出缺乏验证工程师、成本超过潜在风险，以及也许最重要的是，担心等待代码正式验证数周可能会减慢创新速度。

今年早些时候，苹果安全团队表示，在其用于加密的“corecrypto”库中正式验证发现的一些问题无法通过任何其他方式找到。但该公司补充说，在向 corecrypto 添加新代码时必须“保守”，以确保能够跟上审查的步伐。

尚未正式验证任何代码的大公司的两名网络安全高管表示，他们不确定自动化是否值得。但这些未获授权公开发言的高管表示，他们可以想象向主要人工智能实验室支付“经过验证的”人工智能生成代码的费用。

开源软件项目是许多应用程序的基石，其开发人员越来越多地尝试人工智能辅助验证。非营利性人工智能基金会今年利用 Anthropic 的资助来验证与 Sun 在斯坦福大学所做的相同的加密代码。迈克尔·罗森伯格 (Michael Rosenberg) 是名为 curve25519-dalek 的图书馆的维护者，他希望为持续的验证工作提供可持续的资金。 “不过，我不知道这将如何发生，我们当然不应该依赖人工智能公司的善意，”他说。

一些渴望扩大验证的初创公司也不确定是直接向客户部署他们的工具还是通过像 Anthropic 这样的中介机构。他们的总体计划是使用人工智能来自动化定义程序的行为方式所涉及的大部分工作。例如，数据表的规范可能要求它在排序之前和之后包含相同的项目，只是顺序不同。进一步的自动化工作（可能不涉及人工智能）将把代码转换成一种格式，Lean、Rocq 和 Isabelle 等数学工具可以使用它来检查代码是否按预期工作。

另一位最近进入形式验证领域的人是 Madan Musuvathi，他在 20 多年后离开微软研究院，创立了初创公司 Truidic。在诸如 Hugging Face 被 OpenAI 黑客攻击等事件发生后，他觉得迫切需要将他的研究商业化。 “攻击者手中的人工智能可能非常强大，”穆苏瓦蒂说，但验证可以“让人工智能对每个地方的每个人来说都是安全的。”

Proofcraft 是少数长期提供传统验证服务的公司之一，该公司表示，对该过程的日益兴奋正在转化为来自潜在客户的大量询问。该公司首席执行官琼·安德罗尼克 (June Andronick) 和首席科学家格温·克莱因 (Gerwin Klein) 表示，人们的兴趣很容易超过他们和竞争对手所能提供的。

但两人都担心人工智能生成的规范可能会激发对结果的“不合理信任”。验证者也渴望保留他们的工作给他们带来的快乐。克莱因称其“非常容易上瘾，就像益智游戏一样。”如果一切顺利，他将比以往解决更多的问题。
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】斯坦福计算机科学家研究团队在学术前沿与孵化初创企业发布会：运用生成式AI将工业级形式化验证的周期从数月压缩至数小时，大幅削减成本
【起因与机理】解决当下全网AI辅助编程中代码隐蔽逻辑错误频发、不可靠的致命短板
【关键数据与实测】斯坦福大学研究员团队开发出一套基于生成式AI的形式化软件验证工具，成功在半天内以不足500美元的算力成本，完成了过去三名顶级专家耗时五个月才能手工做完的复杂软件数学验证。
【观点态度】依托该科研成果创立的新公司正式亮相，有望重塑严肃软件工程标准。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] Eliminate severe structural and behavioral bugs spawned by unverified, hallucinated code generation
[Key Metrics] Stanford team reduces formal verification from months of human labor to half a day under $500.
[Perspective & Impact] Commercial spin-off launched to establish rigorous guardrails against fragile vibe coding.

items.title: The NYT Cooking app is testing AI recipe modifications
items.title_en: The NYT Cooking app is testing AI recipe modifications
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
The New York Times is testing a new AI feature for its Cooking app that helps users to modify recipes, and it has sparked some drama among users. Last Friday, NYT Cooking senior editor Genevieve Ko announced the feature, which can be used to recommend substitutions for ingredients and cooking equipment, scale recipes to any number of servings, and "generally make our recipes work for what a cook needs at that moment."

items.summary_en: The New York Times is piloting a generative AI tool inside its flagship NYT Cooking application, enabling subscribers to substitute ingredients, swap cookware, and scale servings in real time. While the feature aims to accommodate household kitchens—such as adjusting cook times when substituting baby spinach for kale—it has triggered an immense backlash among loyal foodies. Subscribers decry the algorithmic tinkering, arguing it erodes the craft, credibility, and authority of vetted culinary journalism.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 纽约时报旗下招牌应用《NYT Cooking》近期上线测试一项AI食谱交互改写功能，允许用户针对食材缺失、厨具变化或用餐人数动态微调经典菜谱。例如，当读者询问用菠菜代替羽衣甘蓝时，系统能结合热力学特性提示下锅时机以防软烂，但该举措在忠实读者社群中引发剧烈反弹。大量用户批评机器的随意介入正在稀释专业主厨的烹饪权威与食谱的严谨性，折射出传统生活方式群体对AI渗透日常审美的强烈抵触。

items.title: US antitrust regulators are scrutinizing Nvidia's Hugging Face deal and sales practices
items.title_en: US antitrust regulators are scrutinizing Nvidia's Hugging Face deal and sales practices
items.author: THE DECODER
items.article_content:
The US Justice Department is looking into Nvidia's planned acquisition of open-source platform Hugging Face. According to two sources cited by Reuters, department officials are asking whether the purchase could give Nvidia control over a key hub for distributing AI and hurt its competitors. The deal is worth $12.93 billion, and Nvidia expects it to close in the first half of 2027. The company says Hugging Face will keep supporting partnerships with a range of chip, cloud, and AI providers.

At the same time, US antitrust regulators are investigating Nvidia's acquisitions, investments, sales practices, and possible pressure on customers. The probe started under Joe Biden and has continued under Donald Trump. According to the sources, officials have also looked at Nvidia's acquisitions of SchedMD and Run:ai, along with its licensing deal with Groq. They're also checking whether Nvidia offered customers more AI chips if they bought Nvidia networking gear and Groq processors too.

Nvidia faces scrutiny in Europe as well. France's competition authority is investigating the company over alleged anticompetitive business practices. The regulator is concerned about the industry's dependence on Nvidia's CUDA programming software and about Nvidia's stakes in cloud providers like CoreWeave. It pointed to possible risks such as supply restrictions, unfair contract terms, and discrimination against certain customers.

items.summary_en: The US Department of Justice is probing Nvidia's planned $12.93 billion acquisition of Hugging Face, questioning whether seizing control of the dominant open-source hub would cripple market competition. The bipartisan antitrust investigation extends beyond the platform buyout into prior deals involving Run:ai and SchedMD, alongside licensing agreements. Regulators are actively examining whether Nvidia weaponized its GPU supply dominance through coercive bundling of proprietary networking gear and exclusive partner hardware, with French antitrust regulators pursuing parallel inquiries.

美国司法部正在调查英伟达收购开源平台 Hugging Face 的计划。据路透社援引的两名消息人士称，部门官员正在询问此次收购是否会让英伟达控制一个分发人工智能的关键中心并损害其竞争对手。该交易价值 129.3 亿美元，Nvidia 预计将于 2027 年上半年完成。该公司表示 Hugging Face 将继续支持与一系列芯片、云和 AI 提供商的合作伙伴关系。

与此同时，美国反垄断监管机构正在调查英伟达的收购、投资、销售行为，以及可能对客户施加的压力。该调查始于乔·拜登，并在唐纳德·特朗普的领导下继续进行。据消息人士透露，官员们还关注了英伟达对SchedMD和Run:ai的收购，以及与Groq的授权协议。他们还在调查，如果客户购买了英伟达的网络设备和Groq处理器，英伟达是否会为他们提供更多的人工智能芯片。

英伟达在欧洲也面临着审查。法国竞争主管机构正在调查该公司涉嫌反竞争商业行为。监管机构担心该行业对 Nvidia CUDA 编程软件的依赖，以及 Nvidia 在 CoreWeave 等云提供商中的股份。它指出了可能的风险，例如供应限制、不公平的合同条款以及对某些客户的歧视。

items.title: Anthropic is asking Wall Street to believe in AGI
items.title_en: Anthropic is asking Wall Street to believe in AGI
items.author: The Verge AI
items.article_content:
Today on Decoder, I’m joined by Joey Brookhart, an analyst at the chip and AI research firm SemiAnalysis, to help me dig into the story inside the numbers of the Anthropic IPO filing — a document known as an S-1.

Anthropic just filed its S-1 to go public on the Nasdaq, and it could start trading as soon as next month at a valuation of anywhere between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion. That would immediately make it one of the most valuable companies on the planet.

But the price tag really isn’t the whole story here. The S-1 document published earlier this week is hundreds upon hundreds of pages filled with details that finally paint a picture of the economics of a frontier AI lab. As you might imagine, that picture is both really complicated and built on a series of very, very ambitious assumptions about the future and what AI will do to it.

今天在 Decoder 上，芯片和人工智能研究公司 SemiAnalysis 的分析师乔伊·布鲁克哈特 (Joey Brookhart) 与我一起，帮助我深入了解 Anthropic IPO 文件（一份称为 S-1 的文件）数据中的故事。

Anthropic 刚刚提交了在纳斯达克上市的 S-1 申请，最快可能于下个月开始交易，估值在 1.5 万亿美元至 2 万亿美元之间。这将立即使其成为地球上最有价值的公司之一。

但价格标签并不是故事的全部。本周早些时候发布的 S-1 文件有数百页，其中充满了细节，最终描绘出了前沿人工智能实验室的经济状况。正如你可能想象的那样，这幅图景非常复杂，并且建立在一系列关于未来以及人工智能将对其做什么的非常非常雄心勃勃的假设之上。
